### Milestone 53 — DONE (tick jitter on the Mac VMM, counted in VM exits; 2026-10-18)

The Mac VMM can now vary thread interleavings as hvx does (M43), but it moves timer interrupts by exits, not by branches: the M2 has no PMU clock. **How** (`hvx-mac/hvm.c`, `tjit TJ`): the interrupt of a deadline in tick period k (k = deadline / (CNTFRQ/250), the guest's 4 ms tick) is raised d(k) exits late. d(k) uses hvx's formula and tokens (`tj=`/`tjpm=`/`tjmax=`/`tjlo=`/`tjhi=`, `tjx=k:d`), so `explore.py`'s shrinker works unchanged. The policy is host-side, outside `struct mach`, so it is in neither the snapshot nor the fingerprint. `hvmx` applies it for the workload only and reports `tjk=`/`tjn=`. `hvm` takes `HVM_TJ=<seed>,<permille>,<max>[,<lo>,<hi>]`. `hvm_backend.py` keeps `tj` and caps a generated `tjmax` at 1,000 exits; a busy guest takes about 1,500 exits per tick. **Inert when off:** the M48 boot is still `81711ada76a4a236`, the Redis `disk=none | run` is still `ca13bcd1d77e2b4b` (HVC-idle kernel `2506bb4d…`), and on the network-fault images (`f80c5655…`) main's `hvmx` and this one agree on plain, cut, network and kill schedules. **Limit, measured** (`hvx-mac/race/macrace.c`, once-per-run seat race, two processes; `seeds.sh`): a window with 50 clock reads (exits) was oversold in 10 of 200 seeds, and all 10 repeated exactly; a window of 50,000 iterations of plain work (no exit) was oversold in 0 of 200; with no jitter, neither was. A thread switch can only land at an exit, so windows without exits are out of reach. On this guest kernel every clock read exits, so kernel code, system calls that take time, and Go and Java programs are reachable. Workloads are short in ticks (Redis: 7), so use `--tj-pm 500,1000` on the Mac. `explore.py --backend hvm --timing` on Redis, 40 swarm seeds: 15 of the 17 timed schedules were perturbed, and 16 of 16 failures reproduced. Details: `hvx-mac/explore/README.md` "Tick jitter".

### Milestone 54 — DONE (an 8-defect bug benchmark; five strategies compared; 2026-10-19)

`hvx/bench/` (branch `bug-bench`, merged): d0 = the old front door (`explore-disk.img`), d1–d7 = one realistic defect each patched into a copy of the fixed front door (`patches/`, `build-bench.sh`; images `explore-bench-<name>-disk.img` on the bare-metal machine; an unpatched rebuild is byte-identical to `explore-nf-disk.img` `e5d8d6fb…`): d1 publish to Kafka before MySQL, d2 batched `published` flag, d3 blind retry, d4 a >5 s Kafka send reported "not applied" (needs a slow Kafka + a cut), d5 MyISAM orders table, d6 client treats its own timeout as definite failure, d7 off-by-one Kafka lookup skips the last record. Each confirmed by a hand-written durable-settings trigger that fails twice identically and passes on the control image (`confirm.py`; fingerprints in the README). `run.py` counts a detection only if the schedule passes on the control (the control itself carries the M50 duplicate-in-Kafka bug, `O=kafka@25-30:resp:loss,100%` → order 26 twice, `f1c39a886803a8fa`; never triggered a rejection). **Evaluation** (3 reps × ≤60 runs, early stop, module srcversion `53856EFDC33F55145778DA8`; 100/100 detections reproduced and matched their signature; results `/var/tmp/m46-bench/`): detections out of 24 — random 19, random+new faults 19, swarm 21, swarm+new faults 21, portfolio 20. Every strategy finds the same 7 defects and none finds **d7** (needs a fault covering the end of the workload; a sweep ending its faults at the last order would probably find it). Random fastest on easy defects but misses d0/d4 once each; swarm finds every reachable defect every time but slower (d0 reproduced M42's exact run numbers 17/19/38); the M46 faults add nothing to random and speed swarm on d1/d3/d6 (a plain Kafka kill already produces a send that fails then lands later, which is what d3/d4/d6 need); portfolio best on d4 (3/3, median 21) but slower on easy defects. Also noted: franz-go `ProduceSync` does not honour the request deadline for an in-flight record (the M50 root cause).

### Milestone 55 — DONE (why d7 was missed; end-of-workload sweep; fault-search literature; 2026-10-20)

`--sweep tail` (165 points: every fault kind starting at one of the last 3 orders) finds d7 in 9 minutes. d7 needs Kafka unavailable until the end of the workload (the last order's write is uncertain; its record is the last in the topic, which d7's lookup skips). Per-run trigger probability computed over 1 M generated schedules (`hvx/bench/d7prob.py`): random/swarm effectively never; random+new faults 1 in ~2,800 (~4.3 h); swarm+new faults 1 in ~5,900 (~9 h). A 1,500-run random+nf run hit it at run 1,420 as predicted, but the schedule carried an irrelevant `R=everysec`, so it was classed unsafe-knob — which led to the knob rule (M56). Harness artefact noted: Kafka killed at the last order makes the oracle read Kafka before it restarts ("kafka topic unreadable"). `hvx/explore/RESEARCH-search.md`: literature review (OSDI'14/'18 bug studies: bugs shallow but position-sensitive; random strong vs systematic; Jepsen recurring nemesis; FoundationDB BUGGIFY; CrashMonkey/ALICE crash points; PCT) with five ranked recommendations — items 1–4 done in M56; item 5 (PCT) done on the Mac in M57, with forced points counted in VM exits.

### Milestone 57 — DONE (PCT-style forced preemption points on the Mac VMM; 2026-10-21)

PCT forces thread switches at d-1 random points among the k steps of a run, and its guarantee shrinks as k^(d-1). On the Mac a step is a VM exit, since switches can only happen there, so k is the number of exits. A race in `hvx-mac/race/macrace.c` spans about 20,500 exits, against about a billion branches. **Built:** `hvx-mac/hvm.c` `PCT`: m seeded exits in a range; at each, the timer deadline is made due at once, so the guest takes its tick there and switches if the running thread used its slice (about 2 in 3 points). Thread priorities are not modelled: the guest's scheduler picks. `HVM_PCT=` for `hvm`; `pct=`/`pctn=`/`pctk=` and `pctf=` in `hvmx`. Host-side, off by default; `hvmx` results without the tokens equal main's. **Measured** (200 seeds per cell, `hvx-mac/race/cells.sh`):
- a one-window race of 50 clock reads: jitter 11, 1 point 5, 2 points 6, 10 points 11, **40 points 17**;
- a race needing two such windows: 0 for every strategy in 200; then over 1,000 seeds, **40 points 7** and jitter 0;
- windows of plain work: 0 everywhere.

All 24 hits repeated exactly. Few points (PCT's own setting) did no better than jitter, because a forced point also moves the clock and the guest picks the next thread, so PCT's guarantee does not carry over. Many points did better, and only many points found the two-ordering bug. In the explorer: `explore.py --backend hvm --preempt` gives half the schedules `pct=`/`pctn=`/`pctk=` (ranges `--pct-exits`, default 3,000 and 10,000 exits; RESULT `pctw=` gives the workload length) and drops the Linux-only `pp=`/`xt=` there. On Linux, generated schedules are identical to before. On Redis, 100 swarm seeds: 39 failures, all reproduced, none with durable settings. Details: `hvx-mac/explore/README.md` "Forced preemption points".

### Milestone 58 — DONE (a real bug found by the flush cut; a harness stop-point bug fixed; 2026-10-21)

- **Bug in the order service, found only by cutting power at the k-th FLUSH** (`hvx/cutflush/FINDING.md`). With durable settings and an honest disk, 12 of 282 flush-cut points on `explore-nf-disk.img` and 13 of 118 (k=200..317) on the current front door (`explore-bench-bg-fixed-disk.img`, with the M50 fixes) end `VIOLATION mysql order=N acked but not marked published`; every point re-ran twice with identical fingerprints. Mechanism: the stack's MySQL runs with `skip-log-bin`, and without the binary log InnoDB makes a commit visible to other sessions before its redo fsync completes. The cut stalls the fsync of `UPDATE ... SET published = 1`; the first attempt hits the client deadline; the client's retry (new connection) reads `published = 1`, skips publishing and is ACKed; after recovery the row is not published. The M50 per-order lock does not close it (released when the first request returns on its deadline while its commit still waits). The trace is not a pure power loss (the ACK goes out ~160–200 s of guest time after the cut, because only the data partition loses power); it is the trace of a hung disk followed by a crash, and the same window opens during a normal fsync when two requests for one order overlap. Minimal: `disk=cut dseed=0 cf=204 | run` on explore-nf (`e592e6c6fb6e5f3a`), `disk=cut dseed=0 cf=242 | run` on bg-fixed (`5c04f27153945d7b`). Location: `hvx/stack/main.go` `place`, the branch where `published == 1` goes straight to the ACK. Proposed fixes, untested: commit a real write before ACKing a `published = 1` this request did not write, or run MySQL with the binlog on and `sync_binlog=1`. Results `/var/tmp/m57-cfcheck`.
- **Harness stop-point bug** (explains M56's 2 of 205 non-reproducing fingerprints, and probably M39's one I/O-error outlier): `HVX_GET_CONSOLE` did a 64 KiB `kzalloc` (order 5) that failed under host memory fragmentation (29+ failures in the journal during M56); `console_drain` ignored it, so a failure on the return where the stop marker first appeared made the harness stop one run call late (same verdict, different end state: background MySQL/Kafka writes and timekeeping). Reproduced both outliers bit-for-bit by simulating one dropped read. Fixes: `console_drain`/`console_rebase` retry and then fail loudly (`hvx_stack_verify.c`, merged); the module copies the console straight from `vm->console` with no allocation (`784dee0`; loaded 2026-10-21, srcversion `38E88060EEC5F955DFDFD03`, deploy-metal ALL PASS 25, pinned reproducers unchanged). New diagnostics: `HVX_EXPLORE_DUMP`, `HVX_EXPLORE_RETLOG`, `hvx/explore/statediff.py`. Follow-up (2026-10-21): 14 other harnesses now exit with an error on a failed `HVX_GET_CONSOLE` instead of ignoring it. The two older gaps were re-checked: neither was this cause; the Aug 2026 restore→halt RAM difference no longer reproduces (22 + 8 identical runs; the spread3 guest now needs `tsc=reliable`), and the M34 MySQL durable-disk outlier did not recur in 20 cycles (no allocation failure was logged that day; the first-run-after-reload case is untested).
- **Flush cut** now in the main module (see M56). PCT-style forced preemption on the Mac: see Milestone 57.

### Milestone 59 — DONE (onboarding: configurable guest RAM, liveness properties, Docker/OCI images; 2026-10-21)

All merged; existing manifests build byte-identically, explore.py schedule strings unchanged (16,600), pinned reproducers unchanged.
- **Guest RAM** (`guest.ram_mib`, 256–3072 MiB on Linux, 256–4096 on the Mac; `explore.py --ram-mib`, `hvx_explore --ram-mib` / `HVX_EXPLORE_RAM_MIB`, `hvmx --ram-mib` / `HVM_MEM_MB`): passed to the engine only when not 1024, so default commands are unchanged. Proved at 2048 MiB on both backends (clean + cut twice identical; forcing 1024 fails the example's MemTotal invariant). Example `examples/redis-ram`. Limit: the size is not in the schedule string; a hand-run `hvx_explore one` on a non-default image needs `--ram-mib` (report repro lines and `hydo run` include it).
- **Liveness** (`eventually` properties; `hvx/ASSERTIONS.md`): one record per episode (`ok:true` if satisfied by the deadline), FAIL if any episode misses, NOT EVALUATED if none resolved. ### Milestone 60 — DONE (a replicated system: three-node etcd; a known upstream bug found without being told; 2026-10-22)

`hvx/onboard/examples/etcd/` (`hydo.yaml`, `build.sh [VERSION]` with pinned release-tarball sha256s for 3.6.15 / 3.6.9 / 3.6.8 / 3.5.6 / 3.5.5, `RESULTS.md`). Three members on their own loopback addresses (127.0.0.11/12/13, client/peer ports 2379/2380, 12379/12380, 22379/22380, data `/data/etcd1..3`, each its own user with a per-user source-address route); workload: 30 steps × three concurrent clients doing put + read-back through a rotating member, every 5th step a put followed at once by an online defrag of every member. Invariants: acked puts readable after recovery; each client's revisions never go back (also reported to the console at once); members agree on revision and the last key's `mod_revision`. **Link faults** (new): a service may have `addr:`; `N=a-b@…` (both directions between two services), `N=a-*@…` (isolate one), `O=a-b@…:req|resp:…`; tc u32 on `lo` by source/destination address; `hvx/onboard/hydo-init-links.sh`, spliced into `/sbin/init` only when a manifest uses `addr:`; `manifest_space.py` adds pairs/isolations as targets; arm64 refuses `addr:` for now; existing examples unchanged. All images built with the pinned tools.
**Results** (explore.py `--strategy process --new-faults --timing`, seeds 1–100): 3.6.15, 3.5.6, 3.6.8, 3.6.9: 0 failures; **3.5.5: 19 failures, all reproduced** — 18 members disagree on the revision (e.g. 99/99/98), 1 client revision going back. This is etcd issue 14685 (after an online defrag, a member that crashes replays already-applied entries and its revision diverges), fixed in 3.5.6, which passes the same 100 schedules. Minimal: `disk=cut dseed=4127cc1347fae6ba | run C=30` (`b802065d149ebda2`), `disk=none dseed=890abaea1c4d92d3 | run K=etcd1@10+1 P=etcd3@26+1 T=2:-30` (`20ec47337eaf03f8`). Hand-written check (kill each member after each defrag, 15 schedules): 3.5.5 5 violations, 3.5.6 0. Caveat: the workload was tuned once (a put right before the defrag, so a kill at the next step lands in the window) — a fair "defrag while writes flow" pattern but tuned toward this bug. 3.6.8 vs 3.6.9 (stale reads with a paused leader): no difference found — the process strategy pauses only between steps, never mid-request; needs timed pauses aimed at the leader. Results `/var/tmp/m59-etcd` on the bare-metal machine.

### Milestone 63 — DONE (MySQL binary log on closes the flush-cut finding; Kafka retention deleted acked orders after a clock jump, fixed; 2026-10-22)

Fixes the Milestone 58 finding (`hvx/cutflush/FINDING.md`) in MySQL's configuration, not in the order service. Branch `stack-binlog`. No module change.

**The fix (`build-stack.sh`, `hvx/explore/stack-explore.sh`).** The stack's MySQL ran with `skip-log-bin`. With the binary log off, InnoDB shows a commit to other connections before its redo fsync finishes, so a retry could ACK an order whose `published = 1` was not yet durable. Now `log-bin=binlog`, `sync_binlog=1` (MySQL's default), `server-id=1`, and `innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit=1` stays for the durable setting. With the binary log on, a commit becomes visible only after the prepare (redo fsync) and the binary-log fsync, and crash recovery commits every transaction in the binary log, so anything visible is durable. The relaxed knob (`hydo_flush=off`, explorer `M=0`/`M=2`) now relaxes both logs: `sync_binlog=0` together with `trx_commit=2`/`0`, MySQL's documented fast setting. `build-mysql.sh` (M34) and `hvx/onboard/examples/stack/hydo.yaml` still use `skip-log-bin`; changing them would move unrelated baselines.

**Images** (pinned tools, no M46 stand-ins; a second build is byte-identical): `explore-binlog-pin-disk.img` `ece9a45c…` (the current order service; its `hydostack` is byte-identical to `explore-bench-bg-fixed`'s, `792aab37…`), `explore-binlog-old-pin-disk.img` `3194162a…` (the M39–M46 order service, `hvx/bench/base/main-0112b48.go`), `stack-binlog-pin-disk.img` `2d908c19…` (default stack).

**Proof:**
- **Flush counts.** Each commit now also syncs the binary log. A 30-order workload makes 585 flushes on the current service (was 317) and 491 on the old one (was 281).
- **Flush cuts** (`cf=k`, every k from 200 to the end, results `/var/tmp/m59-binlog` on the bare-metal machine): the current service passed **386 of 386** (before the fix 13 of 118 failed), and the old service passed **292 of 292** (before 12 of 282 failed). Every cut fired. So the configuration alone closes the gap. These runs used the first build of the images, made with the M46 stand-ins; that build has the identical MySQL configuration and differs only in the `hvx_seedrng` binary.
- **Stack checks** on `stack-binlog-pin`, `hvx_stack_verify mode=all`, twice identical, MILESTONE 35 PASS:
  - SANITY `affcc50d0d504a17`;
  - F1 `4e25670bca3d3fd7`;
  - F2 `07ff052d1e8fcd8b` (`VIOLATION mysql order=9`, Kafka has it: the relaxed window, expected; durable `971dedc7b4745fa6`);
  - F3 `35d12da760ad7e12` / `86c31c3bc468cc25`.
  These supersede the M39 stack baselines.
- **Kill list** (`--sweep frontkill`, 40 schedules) on `explore-binlog-pin`: 0 failures.
- **Pinned reproducers** unchanged: `2403499c9a3f8419`, `f87130453609a5d6`.
- **Broad check** on `explore-binlog-pin` (200 swarm schedules with `--concurrency --new-faults --timing`, 2 workers): 125 failures, all reproduced. 124 are in expected classes (lying disk, I/O errors, relaxed settings). One is not, below.

**Second finding, fixed: Kafka deleted acked orders after a large forward clock jump** (`hvx/cutflush/KAFKA-CLOCK.md`). The broad check found one durable-settings failure on `explore-binlog-pin`: Kafka's log started at the first order placed after the guest's realtime clock was stepped forward, and every earlier, ACKed order was gone. Minimal schedule: `disk=none dseed=e80bd3fbb759c1c1 | run K=redis@3+3 N=kafka@21-25:delay,20ms,reorder,11% P=kafka@16+1 T=21:15768000 Q=2d` (`770096791c66765f`, twice).
- **Cause, confirmed with Kafka's log at INFO.** The producer stamps records with the guest's wall clock. Two default settings then act together:
  - after a step of more than 7 days, the next record is over `log.roll.ms` (7 days) past the open segment's first record, so Kafka rolls the segment;
  - the next retention check (first after about 30 s, then every 5 minutes) deletes the closed segment, because its newest record is older than `retention.ms` (7 days). The broker logs "Deleting segment LogSegment(baseOffset=0 …) due to retention time 604800000ms breach" and "Incremented log start offset to 21".
- **The odd threshold.** 6.99 days passes and 7.002 days fails. Above that it is a race between the first retention check and the oracle's read. That is why 90 days passed and 120 failed on one image, while on another image 8 days failed. With a 10-second wait before the oracle, every jump of 7.002 days or more fails.
- **A real deployment would hit it:** any broker whose clock steps forward by more than the retention, such as a machine that boots with its clock far behind and is then corrected by its time service, or a VM restored from an old snapshot. Kafka works as designed; keeping orders in a topic with 7-day retention was the stack's mistake.
- **Fix (`build-stack.sh`):** `log.retention.ms=-1`. On the fixed image, all nine jump sizes up to 365 days pass, twice each. The broad check (seeds 1–60) gave 37 failures, all reproduced, all in expected kinds, and all 22 durable-settings runs passed. New diagnostic switches `STACK_KAFKA_DIAG`, `STACK_ORACLE_WAIT` and `STACK_KAFKA_EXTRA` change nothing when unset.
- **Same exposure elsewhere, left unchanged** because fixing it moves unrelated baselines: the single-Kafka image (`build-linux.sh` §2l) and `hvx/onboard/examples/stack/hydo.yaml`.

**Current stack baselines** (both fixes; pinned tools). Images: `explore-binlog-ret-disk.img` `2d748bd1…` (byte-identical to the investigation's fixed image) and `stack-binlog-ret-disk.img` `b7eb93ee…`. `hvx_stack_verify mode=all`, twice identical, MILESTONE 35 PASS:
- SANITY `ceee1ce465e5424b`;
- F1 `3ddc9bd9aa95cf99`;
- F2 `00af090e634fefb5` (VIOLATION mysql order=9, the relaxed window; durable `df945fb47a53e280`);
- F3 `88fa2915c90b452f` / `e9f60d6301f75013`.

The kill list (40 schedules) gives 0 failures. These supersede the `*-binlog-pin` values above and the M39 stack values. The pinned explorer reproducers (`2403499c9a3f8419`, `f87130453609a5d6`) use older images and are unchanged.

### Milestone 65 — DONE (a rare fingerprint gap was the firmware: SMIs counted on the branch clock; fixed; 2026-10-22)

The gap seen before ("a clean schedule of one example gives a different fingerprint in 1 of 5–10 runs") was found and fixed. A side branch, commits `c370a02` (module) and `f9135bc` (tools), merged as `009ada7`.
- **Cause.** A System Management Interrupt (SMI) runs the firmware's handler with the guest's `IA32_PERF_GLOBAL_CTRL` still loaded, and the PMU branch clock (M33) kept counting the handler's branches: inside the guest `IA32_DEBUGCTL.FREEZE_WHILE_SMM` was 0, because hvx did not use "load debug controls" and every VM exit clears DEBUGCTL. One SMI adds about 225,000–285,000 branches, so the next tick lands early at a host-chosen point. On this bare-metal machine reading one EFI variable causes 4 SMIs; fwupd does that when its daemon starts and during `fwupd-refresh` (every 1–2 hours).
- **Evidence.** Without SMIs: about 67 serve runs and 1 fresh boot all `fe24b9342a961c9f`, every return identical. The only two unexplained outliers of that schedule in the journal since 2026-10-20 overlap an fwupd start (06:38) and an `fwupd-refresh` (07:05). 4 injected SMIs changed exactly the hit runs; the first differing return shows +905,573 branches and one extra tick, every earlier return identical. Counter test `hvx/tdet/smitest.c` (a loop of exactly 400,000,000,000 branches): 356 SMIs gave 101,281,973 too many on the old module, exactly 400,000,000,000 on the fixed one.
- **Fix (`hvx/hvx.c`).** At load hvx checks `PERF_CAPABILITIES` bit 12 (freeze in SMM) and the "load debug controls" entry control; if both, every PMU-clock entry loads `GUEST_IA32_DEBUGCTL = FREEZE_WHILE_SMM` (and DR7 from the register file, 0x400, which is what every exit leaves anyway). The load message ends "freeze in SMM yes/no". VMs without the PMU clock are unchanged.
- **Verified** on a side module `/dev/hvxtd`: 50 of 50 serve runs `fe24b9342a961c9f`, runs with injected SMIs identical, side-metal ALL PASS (25 checks), pinned reproducers unchanged. **Loaded into the main `hvx.ko`** together with M66 (srcversion `C907B1D09F5370F6CC93B45`, dmesg "freeze in SMM yes"; see M66).
- **Confirmed on the main module** (same day, after the reload): 10 serve runs all `fe24b9342a961c9f` (369 return lines identical), and 6 runs with 4 injected SMIs in runs 2, 4 and 6 all identical; results `/var/tmp/m65-tdet/mainA`, `mainB`.
- **Ruled out** (that schedule each time): random host-timed exits plus forced re-entries (module knobs `chaos_ptimer`, `chaos_preempt`, off by default), forced CPU migrations, host memory and CPU pressure, RDRAND/RDSEED (knob `probe_rand`: the guest runs neither).
- **Tools:** `HVX_EXPLORE_RETLOG` also prints the host SMI count; `hvx/tdet/` has `retsplit.py` (first differing return), `smirun.sh` (SMI reproducer), `smicount.py`, pressure/migration helpers, `build-hvxtd.sh`.
- **Open:** fwupd still runs on the bare-metal machine (harmless to the fixed module); older single outliers (M34 MySQL, M39 I/O-error) were not checked against fwupd times.

### Milestone 66 — DONE (several virtual CPUs, stage 1: exact branch-counted turns on hand-written guests; 2026-10-22)

(Numbered 66 because the System Management Mode clock work on main is "M65".) Stage 1 of `hvx/SMP_PLAN.md`; full write-up `hvx/SMP_STAGE1.md`. Built by an agent on a side-by-side module (`hvx/smp/build-hvxsmp.sh`, `/dev/hvxsmp`, bare-metal machine tree `~/hydo-smp`); the main `hvx.ko` was not touched during development.
- **Opt-in:** `HVX_VM_SMP_SCHED` (flags bit 5) with `n_vcpus > 1`. It needs the PMU clock: CREATE_VM returns EINVAL without it.
- **In-kernel round-robin:** one `HVX_RUN`/`HVX_RUNC` runs every vCPU in turns of exactly Q guest conditional branches, or seeded lengths in [1, Q]. The PMU landing target is min(next tick, turn end). A turn ends only where there is no STI/MOV-SS shadow and no half-delivered event. THROTTLE and max_insns stops also wait for such a point, and the THROTTLE count is scheduler state, so stops never depend on where an ioctl returned.
- **One VM clock:** TSC, instruction clock and the tick grid are shared; each vCPU's own branches are counted separately.
- **Halted and spinning vCPUs:** HLT ends the turn, and the vCPU is skipped until an interrupt can be delivered to it. The clock jumps only when every vCPU is halted. K consecutive PAUSE exits end a turn; hardware pause-loop exiting is not used.
- **State:** `HVX_GET_SCHED`/`HVX_SET_SCHED` (ioctls 53/54) carry the scheduler state, the shared clock and per-vCPU cr2, halted and re-injection state; `struct hvx_snapshot` is unchanged. Only vCPU 0 claims the boot-CPU bit. The vCPU index enters the tick-jitter and inserted-tick hashes as 0 for vCPU 0.
- **Fixes along the way (scheduler mode only):** an IPI to a vCPU that was not running was stamped with that vCPU's stale clock; and a stale STI shadow after a stepped-over instruction blocked interrupts. The one-vCPU path keeps the stale-shadow behaviour, because fixing it there would move existing fingerprints. The VM structure is now allocated with `kvzalloc`, because opening the device failed with ENOMEM on a fragmented host.
- **Tests:**
  - `hvx_sched_pmu_test`: per-vCPU branch counts exact (150,000,000 + 50,000,017), 0 overshoots, identical in 3 runs; one tick grid; a snapshot at turn 2,693 of 5,386 gives `73a465516c4e0094` for the straight, continued and restored runs.
  - `hvx_sched_sweep_test`: turn lengths 1..2000 replay and branch-from-snapshot identical at all 894 turn boundaries and at 189 mid-turn stops.
  - `hvx_sched_race_test`: a race in plain computation, with the tick period made huge so no tick falls in the window. 21 of 40 (turn length, seed) cells lose sales; every cell is identical when run twice; grid hash `8cb7c61a2393f44e`. Turns alone hit a window that timer jitter cannot reach.
- **Gate:** `race/side-metal.sh` against the side module: ALL PASS (25 checks), every existing fingerprint unchanged. The same three tests and the same 25 checks passed again on the module merged with main (with the M65 SMM clock freeze), with identical numbers.
- **Loaded into the main `hvx.ko`** on 2026-10-22 (with the M65 SMM clock freeze; srcversion `C907B1D09F5370F6CC93B45`, dmesg "freeze in SMM yes"): `deploy-metal.sh load` ALL PASS (25 checks), every fingerprint unchanged; pinned reproducers `2403499c9a3f8419` / `f87130453609a5d6` unchanged.
- **Not yet:** stage 2 (real Linux with several CPUs: AP start-up by INIT/SIPI, MP table and CPUID topology, device interrupts routed by destination) and stage 3 (explorer tokens for turn lengths). The several-CPU tests are not in `deploy-metal.sh`.

### Milestone 67 — DONE (strategies draw timed kills and k-th-flush power cuts; d10 and d11 found; 2026-10-22)

Closes the M62 gap. Branch `draw-x-cf` (commits `397cef1`, `219dda9`), merged as `59f5546`; only `hvx/explore/` changed (`explore.py`, new `more_faults_ident.py`, `bench_more_faults.py`).

The one candidate found during the runs was the M63 Kafka retention bug (fails on the bench control and `explore-binlog-pin`, OK on `explore-binlog-ret`). Results `/var/tmp/m62-xcf/` on the bare-metal machine.

Now, when the order service is dead at the end of the workload and cannot restart, the guest (`hvx/explore/stack-explore.sh`) leaves the un-ACKed orders un-ACKed, skips the retry and ends the workload; a `cf=` schedule then gets the usual recovery boot and oracle. Branch `guest-avx` (worktree `../hydo-avx`; bare-metal machine tree `~/hydo-avx`, results `/var/tmp/m68-avx`). Built and tested only on the side module `hvxavx.ko` (`/dev/hvxavx`, `hvx/avx/build-hvxavx.sh [load|unload]`); the main `hvx.ko` was not touched.
- **Flag `HVX_VM_X86_64_V3` (flags bit 7; bit 6 is reserved for `HVX_VM_SMP_BOOT`).** Implies v2. CPUID adds XSAVE, OSXSAVE (read from the guest's CR4 at each CPUID), AVX, FMA, F16C, MOVBE (leaf 1), BMI1/AVX2/BMI2 (leaf 7.0), LZCNT (0x80000001) and leaf 0xD for x87|SSE|AVX only (mask 0x7, standard 832-byte area, sub-leaf 1 = 0: no XSAVEOPT/XSAVEC/XSAVES). `HVX_CREATE_VM` returns ENODEV unless the host has AVX2 and XCR0 includes 0x7 (this bare-metal machine: host XCR0 = 0x1f, so XCR0 is switched on every entry and exit).
- **XSETBV** (exit 55) is emulated per vCPU (`hvx_xsetbv`): #GP(0) at CPL > 0, ECX != 0, bit 0 clear, AVX without SSE, or any bit outside 0x7, injected through the re-injection slot; enabling AVX initialises the upper halves (VZEROUPPER in the host). Guest XCR0 is loaded just before VMLAUNCH/VMRESUME and the host's restored just after, with interrupts off. Guest CR4.OSXSAVE is guest-owned (no CR4 mask change).
- **Extended state per vCPU in `fx_page`** (standard-format XSAVE area): XRSTOR after `kernel_fpu_begin`, plain XSAVE at the end of each run with RFBM = guest XCR0 | x87 | SSE. A component XSAVE left in its init state (XSTATE_BV bit 0) gets its init values written, and XSTATE_BV is kept, so the bytes are a pure function of the guest and the next XRSTOR restores the same init tracking. The area is sanitised (XSTATE_BV & 7, header bytes 8..63 zero, MXCSR & 0xffff) before every XRSTOR, since a #GP there is in the host.
- **Snapshot:** `struct hvx_snapshot` gains `xcr0` and `xsave_ext[320]` (bytes 512..831 of the area) at the end; zero for other VMs. The harnesses I touched (`hvx_stack_verify.c`/`hvx_explore`, `hvx_boot_verify.c`) hash them only when `xcr0 != 0`.
- **Wiring:** env `HVX_CPU_V3` (hvx_stack_verify, hvx_boot_verify, hvx_linux), `hvx_explore --cpu v2|v3`, manifest `guest.cpu: v3` (`hydo-build` validates, x86_64 only; nothing else in the image changes), `explore.py --cpu` (default: the manifest's value; adds `--cpu v3` to the engine and to the report's repro line). Generated schedule strings are unchanged against main (3,000 seeds each for the default space and the redis/stack/etcd/miniflux manifests). Fix on the way: `manifest_space.py` gave the generator an empty service list for a manifest without services (division by zero); it now binds a placeholder that `restrict()` drops. `explore.py` on the avx2 image (8 random schedules, `--timing`): all OK, summary `"cpu": "v3"`.
- **Evidence:** `hvx_avx_test` (new, in `deploy-metal.sh`): CPUID values, XGETBV 1 -> 7, five invalid XSETBVs each #GP, YMM0-15 across an HVX_RUN boundary, FMA/F16C/BMI1/BMI2/LZCNT/MOVBE results equal the host's, AVX off/on zeroes upper halves, snapshot restored into a fresh clobbered VM equals the straight run; `3bb428a134ce542a` in every pass; flag off: no XSAVE/AVX in CPUID and XSETBV still exits to userspace. `side-metal.sh` on `/dev/hvxavx`: ALL PASS (25 checks), every fingerprint unchanged; pinned reproducers `2403499c9a3f8419` / `f87130453609a5d6` unchanged.
- **Real Linux** (`examples/avx2`, image `explore-ob-avx2-disk.img` `68267cf4…`, two builds identical): the guest kernel prints "x86/fpu: Enabled xstate features 0x7, context size is 832 bytes, using 'standard' format", `/proc/cpuinfo` lists avx avx2 fma f16c bmi1 bmi2 movbe abm xsave, glibc 2.39 reports "x86-64-v3 (supported)"; a static four-thread AVX2+FMA program checks its vector results against scalar code in 8 steps. INIT resets the target's LAPIC and makes it wait again; STARTUP with vector V starts a waiting vCPU in real mode at V<<8:0, and a second STARTUP is ignored. This needs the unrestricted-guest control, CR0.PE/PG no longer forced, and the 64-bit entry control following the guest's EFER.LMA.

### Roadmap — booting Linux as L2 (phased; from a planning pass over hydo's KVM boot path)

The KVM monitor already boots Linux; hvx must replicate its recipe. Key facts to reuse (from `src/boot.rs`/`src/detlinux.rs`): 64-bit **bzImage** protocol — protected-mode kernel loaded at `0x100000`, **entry `0x100200` directly in 64-bit long mode** (so we DO NOT need real-mode entry or the unrestricted-guest control — a major de-risk), `boot_params`/zero-page @`0x10000` (`RSI`), e820 + cmdline @`0x20000` (`console=ttyS0 earlyprintk=ttyS0 loglevel=8 nokaslr acpi=off`), MP table @`0x9FC00`, initial long-mode GDT/paging (PML4→PDPT→PD with 512×2 MiB identity), CPUID/MSR **synthesized deterministically** (hvx owns CPUID now). Remaining phases, smallest-first:

2. ~~Guest RAM beyond 2 MiB~~ — **DONE (M11)**.
3. ~~Deterministic CPUID + MSR emulation~~ — **DONE (M12)**. Reason 10 → fixed synthetic table (FPU/PAE/APIC/FXSR/SSE/SSE2, LM+NX; no XSAVE/AVX); RDMSR/WRMSR (31/32) → EFER via `GUEST_IA32_EFER`, IA32_TSC via the virtual TSC, curated software store for STAR/LSTAR/CSTAR/SFMASK/KERNEL_GS_BASE/MISC_ENABLE/SYSENTER_*, unknown MSR reads 0 / drops write. Folded into the snapshot+fingerprint.
4. ~~Full privileged-state persistence across runs + `HVX_GET/SET_SREGS`~~ — **DONE (M13)**. Software `struct hvx_sregs` (all CRs, EFER, DR7, 6 segs+LDTR+TR, GDTR/IDTR) seeded on CREATE, loaded in `setup_vmcs`, VMREAD-saved on exit; folded into snapshot+fingerprint; kernel GET/SET_SREGS handlers implemented. Loader notes honored: `fixed_cr()` still ORs the CR0/CR4 FIXED bits; raw `0xffffffff` segment limits; module TR seeded (sel 0x18/base `GPA_TSS`/limit 0x67/ar 0x8b), LDTR forced unusable (ABI `ar` is u16). (The `kernel_fpu_begin/end` guard bundled here is now **DONE (M14)**; the M13 segment-AR-truncation assumption was also corrected in **M14** via `seg_ar()`. Optionally holding VMXON across ioctls, CPU-pinned, for single-step throughput remains a deferred optimization.)
5. ~~Wire up the bzImage loader → first Linux serial output~~ — **DONE (M14)**. Free-run boots the NixOS 6.6.35 bzImage through the decompressor + full early kernel init (version banner, e820, MP-table/RAMDISK parse) to the LAPIC-MMIO wall; four kernel fixes landed (FPU guard, hide CR4.VMXE, reflect FS/GS-base MSRs into the VMCS, `seg_ar()` unusable-segment round-trip). `HVX_GET_CONSOLE` shows the earlyprintk/"Decompressing Linux"/kernel banner. `build-linux.sh` stages the bzImage+initramfs.
6. ~~**LAPIC/IOAPIC** + timer → boot to the initramfs shell~~ — **DONE (M15)**. Not by trapping LAPIC MMIO but by **forcing x2APIC** (LAPIC emulated through the RDMSR/WRMSR trap, MSRs 0x800–0x8FF) + a KVM hypervisor signature (so Linux keeps x2APIC without IR), a minimal IOAPIC/PIC/16550 model, the TSC-deadline timer wired onto M8 injection with an interruptibility gate + LAPIC in-service/EOI, and loading the guest SYSCALL/KERNEL_GS_BASE MSRs into hardware around each run. Reaches the busybox `~ #` prompt (output side). `HVX_CONSOLE_SZ` bumped to 64 KiB. **P6.4 (serial input → interactive shell) — DONE (M18)**: a UART RX ring + `HVX_PUT_INPUT` + COM1 IRQ via `redir[4]` through the M8 path makes the shell interactive (typed/scripted commands run and echo); the transient input ring is kept out of the snapshot, so the M16 fingerprint `1bdf266a0db52bf7` is unchanged.
7. ~~**Determinism harness**~~ — **DONE (M16)**, in FAST free-run (single-step bisection deferred to the PMU milestone below, and moot here — free-run is already fully deterministic, no divergence to bisect). `hvx_boot_verify.c` fingerprints the full end state (console + snapshot + 256 MiB RAM); two fresh boots AND a mid-boot branch are bit-identical (`1bdf266a0db52bf7`), past the KVM RDTSC-calibration wall. Required three determinism fixes: deterministic THROTTLE cadence (retired exits only), deterministic virtual-TSC creep (moved to the retired block so `vm->tsc` is a pure function of `icount`, not perturbed by host interrupts), and the 16550 UART latch added to the snapshot. **Next milestone — PMU fast instruction clock: attempted, BLOCKED by hardware (see the "Milestone 17 — BLOCKED" section above).** The port of `src/pmu.rs`'s `step_insn_fast` (guest-only INST_RETIRED.ANY counter) needs a vPMU in L1; the capability probe found the nested L1 has NO architectural PMU (CPUID.0AH=0, PMU MSRs #GP) because the L0 CPU is **hybrid** (i7-13700HX) and KVM hardcodes guest-PMU-off on hybrid silicon — reloading `kvm` with `enable_pmu=1` succeeds (all rc=0) yet `enable_pmu` stays `N`, so it is NOT a config toggle. The VMX load/save-`PERF_GLOBAL_CTRL` controls ARE present, so the design is directly implementable on a non-hybrid host. On THIS bare-metal machine, stay on the exact MTF clock (M5); whole-boot free-run determinism (M16) does not need the fast clock. Expected walls once on a vPMU-capable host: nested-counting correctness (the M5 MTF cross-check), then LAPIC-timer phase / jitter entropy.

**Risks (nested L1):** guest with IF=1 + long boot takes many external-int exits — the `sti;nop;cli` service window must let L1's host handler run or L1 RCU-stalls (restart via `run-l1.sh`); keep IRQ-off batches bounded (the 65536-exit THROTTLE cap means many re-entries, so Phase 4 state save/restore must be correct first); always surface exit reason+qualification+`guest_phys` for early faults; expect many L1 restarts on triple-faults.

## Key files

- `README.md` — full architecture & usage (authoritative).
- `src/vmm.rs` — determinism engine: clocks, single-step + PMU fast-path (`step_insn_fast`), instruction-counted interrupt injection, snapshot/restore.
- `src/state.rs` — full-state Snapshot + canonical BLAKE3 fingerprint + disk save/load.
- `src/pmu.rs` — guest-only perf counters + overflow/descheduling handling.
- `src/detlinux.rs` — the Linux divergence harness (`boot-verify`).
- `src/boot.rs` / `src/linux.rs` / `src/uart.rs` — the real-Linux boot path.
- `src/verify.rs`, `src/pv.rs`, `src/det.rs`, `src/serial.rs`, `src/memory.rs`, `src/main.rs`.
- `hvx/` — the from-scratch VT-x hypervisor kernel module. `hvx.c` (the module: VMX/EPT + `/dev/hvx` char device + deterministic RDTSC + MTF instruction clock + instruction-clock TSC + in-kernel CPUID/MSR emulation + privileged-state (sregs) persistence + x2APIC/IOAPIC/16550 device model + M18 serial input + M19 deterministic SMP (per-vCPU/shared-VM split, `HVX_SET_VCPU`, instruction-quantum round-robin, cross-vCPU IPIs) + **M20 deterministic virtio-PCI block device: transport-agnostic virtio-blk core (`struct hvx_vblk`, one split virtqueue against a snapshot-able backing image, `virtio_blk_process`), instruction-timed completion via the M8 path, Phase-A PIO doorbell + Phase-B PCI config (0xCF8/0xCFC) + modern virtio-pci MMIO BAR (`hvx_virtio_mmio`) + INTx-through-IOAPIC (`vblk_irq`); `HVX_SET_DISK` also maps the 4th GiB into the guest PT so a hand-written guest can reach MMIO; inert with no disk so the boot is byte-identical; **M21 MSI-X: MSI-X capability/table/PBA in BAR0 + edge LAPIC delivery of the queue vector at the instruction-timed completion (`vblk_msix_irq`), an Intel host bridge at 00:00.0 (`hvx_pci_read_bridge`) so Linux's conf1 sanity check accepts the bus, the HLT handler jumps the clock to a pending disk completion so an idle disk read wakes, and `HVX_DISK_NO_IDMAP` so a real OS's page tables are not poked — real Linux binds `virtio_blk` over MSI-X and reads `/dev/vda`**; **M22 deterministic disk fault injection: a seeded splitmix64 PRNG (`fault_mix`/`fault_roll`) keyed by the per-device request index drives `vblk_fault_decide` in `virtio_blk_process` — delay/error/drop/torn per request + seeded Fisher-Yates completion reorder — `HVX_SET/GET_FAULT`, all fault state folded into the snapshot, inert (byte-identical to M21) when disabled**; **M23 deterministic virtio-net PCI device: a SECOND virtio-PCI function at dev 4 (`struct hvx_vnet`, vendor 0x1af4/device 0x1041) with two virtqueues [receiveq/transmitq], MSI-X, MAC+VERSION_1 (minimal features, NO F_STATUS so the link comes up RUNNING), scripted RX via `HVX_PUT_RX` delivered by MSI-X at an instruction-timed completion (`virtio_net_rx_deliver`/`vnet_msix_irq`), TX captured via `HVX_GET_TX` (`virtio_net_tx_process`), `HVX_NET_ATTACH` [pokes the same `pdpt[3]` A/D-preset idmap as the disk], and an opt-in `HVX_NET_PACED` run-loop RX trickle so real Linux answers a scripted ARP; all virtio-net + RX-FIFO + captured-TX state folded into the snapshot, inert when no net device attached**; **M24 deterministic network fault injection: a seeded PRNG (`net_fault_roll`/`net_reorder_roll`, reusing the M22 `fault_mix`) keyed by direction + per-direction packet index drives `vnet_fault_decide` in `virtio_net_rx_deliver`/`virtio_net_tx_process` — per-packet drop/delay(RX)/corrupt/duplicate + seeded Fisher-Yates used-ring reorder on RX and TX — `HVX_SET/GET_NET_FAULT`, all net-fault state folded into the snapshot, inert (byte-identical to M23) when disabled; the non-paced RX kick now drains the whole batch [`max_consume` param] so the fault engine sees a multi-packet batch, paced/single-frame paths stay one-per-kick**; **M26 flush-aware DROP + bigger disk: `HVX_FAULT_DROP_UNFLUSHED` holds a rolled write in a per-device VOLATILE WRITE CACHE (`struct hvx_vblk.unsync[]` + a lazily-`kvmalloc`'d buffer) that a `VIRTIO_BLK_T_FLUSH` commits (durable) — `virtio_blk_process` stashes/overlays[read-your-writes]/invalidates/commits, `VIRTIO_BLK_F_FLUSH` advertised only when the class is armed, cache cleared on `HVX_SET_DISK`/reset; `HVX_DISK_MAX` 1 MiB→64 MiB. All additive + inert when the class is disabled, so every prior fingerprint holds**; **M27 deterministic idle heartbeat: when the guest idle-HLTs fully tickless (`tsc_deadline==0`, no pending completion) AND the VM set `HVX_VM_IDLE_HEARTBEAT` (`struct hvx_config.flags`, ex-`_pad`, default off → `vm->idle_hb`), the run-loop advances the virtual clock by `HVX_IDLE_HEARTBEAT_TSC` and injects the LAPIC-timer vector — a synthetic tick that runs Linux's timer ISR + softirqs [loopback delivery] + the scheduler, so a co-located loopback service [redis] blocked in `epoll_wait` does not deadlock. OFF by default so every prior boot — incl. the no-disk baseline that also idles unarmed — is byte-identical**; **M28 Rung-3 scale-up: the backing disk is a PAGE ARRAY (`struct hvx_vblk.disk_pages[]`+`n_disk_pages`, the M11 recipe — `vblk_disk_alloc`/`_free`/`_from_user`/`_to_user`, `disk_write_bytes`, page-split `vblk_disk_rw`) + a zero-copy disk `mmap` window (`hvx_disk_fault`/`hvx_disk_ops` at `vm_pgoff >= HVX_DISK_MMAP_PGOFF`, dispatched by `hvx_mmap`); sandbox-flaky AOF test), `build/hvx_seedrng` (the deterministic CRNG seeder, static musl like hydokv), a byte-reproducible empty ext2 `build/redis-disk.img` (same pinned `libfaketime`-frozen `mke2fs` `hydo_phase=` on the cmdline: `solo` [workload+oracle, no crash], `workload` [SETs over `127.0.0.1` then `SIGSTOP` redis], `oracle` [AOF-replay + oracle] — brings up `lo`, seeds the CRNG, runs redis busybox + `/sbin/init`, built via `mke2fs -t ext4 -d` in a SIMPLE layout [`-O ^metadata_csum,^64bit,^flex_bg,^resize_inode`] + a pinned-`python3` pass that ZEROES every inode's `i_ctime` — the one images), `build/rootfs-data.img` (a small reproducible ext2 rw-data disk via `mkext2_reproducible`), `build/rootfs-disk.img` (the two partitions assembled behind a hand-crafted deterministic MBR: p1 ext4 ro-root @ LBA 2048, p2 ext2 rw-data @ LBA 1050624), and `build/initramfs-rootfs.cpio.gz` (the virtio-blk + `crc32c_generic` + ext4/jbd2/ext2 module stack + an `/init` that mounts `/dev/vda1` ext4 `ro,noload`, `mount --move /dev`s into the new root, and `switch_root`s; the real root's `/sbin/init` mounts `/dev/vda2` ext2 rw, runs the committed-record workload + oracle → `HYDO-ORACLE` + `hydo-rootfs-marker`). Two-build sha256 identity: `rootfs-ext4.img`=`6df9f82c…`, `rootfs-disk.img`=`a4aefaf1…`. **M30** (§2j) stages the Rung-4 multi-service system assets: `build/hydoapp` (the static-musl app tier + client, built with the same pinned musl gcc as hydokv/seedrng), a byte-reproducible empty ext2 `build/system-disk.img` (`mkext2_reproducible` with a distinct UUID/hash_seed + a python pass that ZEROES all superblock/inode time fields — see below), and `build/initramfs-system.cpio.gz` (virtio-blk + ext2 stack + redis + hydoapp + seedrng + an `/init` with `solo`/`workload`/`oracle` phases via `hydo_phase=`, `hydo_fsync=` that bring up `lo`, seed the CRNG, start redis + the app tier, and drive the client→app→redis workload/oracle over `127.0.0.1`). §2h (redis) is byte-untouched. The `system-disk.img` time-zeroing pass fixes a latent `libfaketime`-advance jitter that made this image's mke2fs timestamps land on different seconds across builds (the existing images happen to complete inside one second; this one straddled a boundary) — localized to §2j so no existing image moves. ### Milestone 70 — DONE (freeze a service at an exact packet of its traffic; 2026-10-23)

Branch `freeze-call` (commits `1398f27`..`9a027c3`), merged as `4832a82`. Userspace and build only.
- **Token** `F=<svc>><peer>@<step>[#<n>][:<match>]:<dur>` (`>` = packets `<svc>` sends to `<peer>`, `<` = packets it receives): from workload step `<step>`, at the n-th such packet (optionally only packets containing `<match>`), stop `<svc>`'s whole process tree for `<dur>` ms of guest time. `#0` fires nothing and prints a compact traffic trace (`hydo-fc-trace:`) to pick n. A static helper (`hvx/onboard/hydo_fc.c`, pinned musl gcc) runs SCHED_FIFO, holds the matched packet in a netfilter queue, stops the tree, waits until every thread is stopped, then releases the packet, so the service cannot run past it. Opt-in: `freeze` in the manifest's `faults:` (plus optional `freeze_match:`); `hydo-build` then stages the helper, a pinned `iptables` (`/nix/store/xnrrq638…-iptables-1.8.10`) and the netfilter modules, and splices `hvx/onboard/hydo-init-freeze.sh` into the init. Other manifests build byte-identically.

### Milestone 71 — DONE (lifting a network fault drains the netem queue; 2026-10-23)

Branch `netem-drain` (commits `0be22e6`, `5b673b4`, `2bea519`), merged. Guest scripts only.
- **Cause:** deleting a netem qdisc in kernel 6.6.35 discards its delay queue (`netem_reset` → `tfifo_reset`); `tc qdisc change` keeps it. `net_off` in `hvx/onboard/hydo-init.sh` (used by `N=`, `O=` and the `addr:` link faults), four heals in `hvx/explore/stack-explore.sh` and the stack's `hydo_net=` mode in `build-stack.sh` deleted at once.
- **Fix:** `net_heal` (in `hydo-init.sh`, a copy in `build-stack.sh`'s init): change the netem to `rate 100gbit corrupt 0%` (no delay or loss; queued packets keep their send times and order), wait in guest time until the queue is empty (bound: delay + 4 × jitter + 500 ms), remove the filters, wait ≤ 50 ms, delete. Console line `queued=<n> drained_ms=<ms> left=<n>`. After a heal new packets wait behind queued ones (order kept, at most one delay).
- **Evidence:** `examples/redis/hydo-netem.yaml` (Redis + invariant `RetransSegs == 0`): `N=redis@3-6:delay,300ms` VIOLATION retrans=2 on main's init (`c568d85e8e4f70ba`, twice) → OK retrans=0 with 2 packets drained (`5b226954f8df4479`); `O=redis@3-6:resp:delay,300ms` → OK `dd440bce5c239ea2`; `N=redis@5-20:delay,300ms` → OK `3ed5964ccdd8e5f4`. etcd 3.6.15 link faults drained 34, 37 and 6 packets with 0 lost. Without network faults, verdict kinds unchanged; Redis `C=12 R=everysec` now loses `k:2` (was `k:4`), stack `disk=cut C=20 M=2` names order 9 (was 0) — timing shift from the longer init, not proven.
- **Images** (`~/hydo/build` on the bare-metal machine, each two builds identical): `explore-binlog-ret-xr-nq-disk.img` `4a6a8493…` (current stack explorer image; vs `-xr` only `/sbin/init` and `/etc/stack-explore.sh` differ; 40 swarm `--new-faults --durable-only` 0 failures, 9 of 21 heals had queued packets, none lost), `explore-ob-redis-netem-nq-disk.img` `c7bc532a…`, `explore-ob-redis-nq-disk.img` `03beff6c…`, `explore-ob-etcd-3.6.15-nq-disk.img` `021d350a…`, and main-init comparison images `explore-ob-{redis-netem,redis,etcd-3.6.15}-main-disk.img`. Results `/var/tmp/nq`.
- **Open:** older onboarding images with network or link faults keep the old behaviour until rebuilt; the default stack image's next build needs its M63 baselines re-measured.

### Milestone 73 — DONE (M70 follow-up: recovery clock; freeze measurement; 2026-10-23)

Branch `freeze-call-2` (from `3762613`). Userspace, build and docs only; no module change.
- **The 7 blind hits of M70 are not the bug M70 reproduced.** All have a power cut after the last step (`C=10`); the acknowledgement was processed only in the recovery boot, whose clock restarted at `guest.clock_start`, so it looked earlier than events the first boot had written. Only the check that compares those times failed; the other checks passed. `disk=cut dseed=0 | run C=10` alone reproduces it (twice `b4b7098cc190070b`); the shrinker reduced seed 12 to `C=10` and seed 20 to `C=10 P=kafka@3+1`. The process strategy still does not find that bug blind.
- **Freeze changes:** `freeze_match:` may be `replies:` / `requests:` lists, and a drawn string uses its own direction; peer `workload` (the workload's client) for a project whose services do not call each other (`examples/redis/hydo-freeze.yaml`). Identity checks (`freeze_call_ident.py`, `manifest_space_ident.py`, `more_faults_ident.py`) pass against main.

### Milestone 74 — DONE, NEGATIVE RESULT (do several vCPUs find races that one vCPU misses? 2026-10-23)

Two experiments on the main `hvx.ko` with several vCPUs (M66, M69), by two agents. Write-ups `hvx/bench/SMP-RESULTS.md` and `hvx/knownbugs/sqlite/README.md` (new section). Tools: `hvx/bench/run.py` and `confirm.py` take `--vcpus N --turns`, and `hvx/knownbugs/sqlite/hunt.py` takes `--vcpus N --turns`, weighted toward short turns. Without the new flags the schedule strings are unchanged (5,760 and 36,000 strings checked). `hvx_explore` gained two read-only per-vCPU statistics prints on stderr: the scheduler counters (`schedstat`) and `HVX_EXPLORE_VCPUSTAT`. Results on the bare-metal machine: `/var/tmp/bench2`, `/var/tmp/sqlsmp`.

**Benchmark race defects** (images `explore-bench-m59-*-pin`; swarm, 3 repetitions of up to 60 runs; run of first detection per repetition):

| defect | 1 vCPU, concurrent clients | 2 vCPUs + turns, concurrent clients | 1 vCPU, no concurrent clients | 2 vCPUs + turns, no concurrent clients |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| d8 (no per-order lock) | 5, 2, 46 | 5, 2, 46 | 0/3 | 0/3 |
| d9 (Redis connection unlocked) | 5, 31, 1 | 5, 31, 8 | 0/3 | 0/3 |
| d12 (shared Kafka key buffer) | 5, 2, 1 | 5, 2, 1 | 23, 19, 1 | 18, 13, 1 |

- **Checks:**
  - All 33 detections re-ran with the same fingerprint, matched their signature, and passed on the control.
  - The second CPU was really used: every 2-vCPU boot printed "Brought up 1 node, 2 CPUs", and vCPU 1 retired 13–733 M branches per run.
  - The identical run numbers have one cause: in those schedules the concurrent clients trigger the defect whatever the vCPU count.
  - d9's run 8 on 2 vCPUs: the run-1 crash did happen, but its restart could not reach Kafka, so it counted as a harness error.
- **Random strategy, 2 vCPUs, concurrent clients:** d8 4, 1, 7; d9 1, 1, 2; d12 1, 1, 2. Random with 2 vCPUs and no concurrent clients was stopped early (d8 not found in 79 runs).
- **Details:**
  - d9 with `Q=2` crashes on 2 vCPUs in 6 of 9 turn settings, but 1 vCPU with tick jitter or inserted ticks crashes it too, in 5 of 10.
  - Some d12 schedules fail only on 2 vCPUs: seed 2013, the same string, fails on 2 and passes on 1. That gives slightly earlier detections, too few repetitions to call it a speed-up.
  - A 2-vCPU run cost about 3× a 1-vCPU run (about 43 s against 15 s, bare-metal machine load varied).
- **Verdict:** d8 and d9 need two requests for the same order at once; extra CPUs cannot create that. d12 is found both ways at similar speed.

**SQLite 3.51.2 WAL-reset bug, blind** (`hvx/knownbugs/sqlite/`):
- **Turn mix.** Each turn end costs about 0.8 ms of host time. On the heaviest workload a run takes 13 s with default turns, 32 s at q=10,000, 216 s at q=1,000, and over 900 s at q≤300. So the mix per schedule is 5% default turns, 15% long, 70% q=1,000–10,000 (half seeded), and 10% q=300–999.
- **Runs:**
  - 2 vCPUs: 144 runs in 3.5 hours, 19.1 M turn switches, 80 M checkpoints, 0 violations.
  - 4 vCPUs with the short mix: 32 runs in 1.8 hours, 0 violations.
  - 4 vCPUs with default turns: 912 runs in 46 minutes, 0 violations.
- **Sanity checks:** "Brought up 2/4 CPUs"; walrace threads seen on every CPU (vCPU 0 retired 19.5 G branches, vCPU 1 28.1 G); runs identical from a fresh boot and from the snapshot (`3173108c39ad8004`, `958429cf955867e6`, `6cac0c27871d3ad9`).
- **Verdict:** not found. Short turns are too expensive for this window at an affordable budget, and the workload rarely produces the trigger; native runs on 4 real cores also missed it in about 5,800 seeds.
- **Possible next steps (not started):** make the workload reset the WAL far more often; make turn ends cheaper, or use short turns only around WAL activity.

**Overall:** on these targets, several vCPUs found nothing that one vCPU with concurrent clients, tick jitter or inserted ticks does not find. They work and are deterministic, but buy no new reach here. Lesson about cost: the benchmark experiment ran 13.5 hours because cells whose outcome was already clear kept running; set a time limit and check halfway.

### Milestone 75 — DONE (the Linux release: one `hydo` command and a self-contained tarball for x86_64 + VT-x; 2026-10-23)

Branch `linux-release` (worktree `../hydo-lrel`, rebased on `d9cefa7`; not merged). Userspace, packaging and docs; no module change. Files: `hvx/dist/` (`hydo`, `install.sh`, `build-release.sh`, `libexec/{hvx-run,faketime,bin/debugfs}`, `assets.sha256`, `README.md` for maintainers, `QUICKSTART-linux.md` shipped as the release's README). Two small changes to existing tools, both inert by default: `explore.py` reads `HYDO_BUILD` / `HYDO_HVX_RUN` / `HYDO_SNAP_DIR` (defaults `~/hydo/build`, `~/bin/hvx-run`, `/var/tmp/hvx-snap`) and, with `HYDO_CLI`, prints a `hydo run` hand-reproduction line; `explore/ptedges.h` compiles without libipt under `-DHYDO_NO_LIBIPT`.
- **The command** (same verbs as the Mac release): `hydo doctor` (Intel + `vmx`, bare metal, a usable non-hybrid PMU or "exit-count clock is used", Python 3.9+, `cc`/`make`/`flock`/`xz`/`sudo`/`modinfo`, password-less sudo, kernel headers, lockdown, module built/loaded/same `srcversion`, `kvm_intel` not loaded, release files, disk space); `hydo module build|load|unload|status [--name N] [--dry-run]` (exclusive `flock` on `~/.hvx-module.lock` = `$HYDO_LOCK`, the bare-metal machine's `hvx-run`/`hvx-reload` convention; `load` removes `hvx`, `kvm_intel`, `kvm` then `insmod`; `--name` builds and loads a side copy with its own device and lock file, never touching `hvx` or KVM; `status` reads lock holders from `/proc/locks` without taking the lock); `hydo build` (imports `hydo-build`); `hydo run [IMG] "<schedule>"` (`hvx_explore one` under the shared lock, engine options from the image's manifest, writes `run.json`); `hydo repro <run dir | explore dir | schedule>` (re-runs from a fresh boot and compares fingerprints); `hydo explore` (`explore.py`, default 20 seeds, 2 workers); `hydo report`.
- **No Nix for users.** The release carries the guest kernel and `initramfs-kafka.cpio.gz` (sha256 `0a9ede35…`, `d074d764…`), busybox 1.37.0, `hvx_seedrng` compiled with the pinned musl gcc (comes out as the pinned `c2a440c5…`), `hydo_fc`, the guest's netem/u32/netfilter modules, the iproute2 + iptables closures as one GNU tar with the store's read-only modes, and e2fsprogs 1.47.0 + libfaketime 0.9.10 with their glibc. `libexec/faketime` runs the Nix-built `mke2fs`/`debugfs` with the bundled loader (`--library-path`, `--preload libfaketime.so.1`). `hydo build` points `hydo-build` at these through its `HYDO_*` variables, a module-local `os` view and a replacement `closure()`; `root.nix:` still needs `nix-store`. `build-release.sh` fetches every asset in one remote session from the build machine (all gc-rooted pins), checks 34 files against `assets.sha256`, and builds a 45 MB tarball offline; `install.sh` checks `SHA256SUMS`, unpacks the store tar, compiles `hvx_explore` (with libipt if present) and the module, and runs doctor. It never loads the module.
- **Image reproducibility across machines (three findings).** With `HYDO_KEEP_OWNERS=1`, the release on the NixOS build machine builds the Redis and Redis-netem images byte-identical to a plain pinned `hydo-build` (root `bcea6b1d…`, netem root `6d768c1c…`, data disks `2d52cd04…`, `6b1dab4d…`). On the Ubuntu bare-metal machine the first builds differed in 8 bytes: the mtimes of 4 inodes were 4 hours apart. Cause: libfaketime reads hydo-build's `FAKE_TS` "2020-09-13 16:26:40" in the local zone, and it equals `FIXED_MTIME` 1600000000 only in the build machine's zone (UTC+4); so even a plain `hydo-build` gives different bytes in another zone. The wrapper sets `TZ=UTC-4`. The build also ignores the machine's `/etc/mke2fs.conf` (`MKE2FS_CONFIG` names no file; Ubuntu has one, NixOS does not), fixes the umask at 022 (Ubuntu's 002 changed directory modes), and sets every root inode's owner to 0:0 with `debugfs` (mke2fs -d records the builder's uid/gid). After that the Ubuntu bare-metal machine (no Nix, UTC, umask 002) and the NixOS build machine build the same bytes for the repository's Redis manifests: root `aec24305…`, netem root `b0fe5081…`.
- **Quickstart on the bare-metal machine** (clean install into `~/hydo-lrel/prefix2`; repeated after the rebase with tarball `373c609a…` in `~/hydo-lrel/prefix3`, same image sha and fingerprints; doctor "all checks passed"; the Redis example with `files/` sources): image `8c828d3e…` (two fresh build directories identical); `disk=none | run` OK acked=20, `c513f10aee733aae` twice; `disk=cut | run C=12 R=everysec` VIOLATION key k:2 lost, `ecef6f8fe6c39ec0` twice; Redis-netem `N=redis@3-6:delay,300ms` OK retrans=0, `e518f6b9fd845ee5` twice.
- **Explore + repro** (earlier install, same code; image built in a directory whose staged root was first made under umask 002, so its sha differs: `05db0de2…`): `hydo explore --seeds 1-20 --strategy swarm` (2 workers, 506 s on a loaded bare-metal machine): 11 failures, all expected classes (io-errors 3, lying-disk 6, unsafe-knob 2), 11/11 reproduced by the explorer, 4 minimal schedules each twice identical; `hydo repro hydo-out/explore` re-ran all 11 failures and 4 minimal schedules from fresh boots: **15 of 15 with the recorded fingerprint**. `hydo repro <run dir>` reproduced the cut run.
- **Module handling** (main module never touched; srcversion stayed `CA5BF8BF2A0D66B312A68EF`): `status` reported the loaded `hvx` as the release's source; `load`/`unload --dry-run` printed `sudo rmmod hvx && sudo insmod …` and `sudo rmmod hvx`; a side module `hvxlrel` built, loaded (`/dev/hvxlrel`), and unloaded; with a shared holder on its lock, `unload` waited 7 s until the holder finished.
- **Not done:** runs use `sudo` (no udev rule for `/dev/hvx`); AMD is not supported; a staged root directory left by an earlier non-release build keeps its old directory mode (the reason for the `05db0de2…` image above); the Mac release (`hvx-mac/dist/build-release.sh`) copies only `hydo-init.sh` of the init extensions, so an arm64 build of a manifest with `eventually` invariants or `guest.clock_after_cut` would fail to find `hydo-liveness.sh` / `hydo-init-clock.sh` (not checked, not fixed).

### Milestone 76 — DONE (the freeze sweep: every packet point of a run; 2026-10-24)

Branch `freeze-sweep` (from `2e0e3fe`, rebased onto `cd5e551`); only `hvx/explore/explore.py`, `hvx/explore/manifest_space.py` (sweep kind `freeze`) and `hvx/onboard/MANIFEST.md` changed. No module or image change; `hvx_explore` compiled from main in `~/hydo-fsw` (identical binary to `~/hydo-fc`'s). Results `/var/tmp/m74-fsw` on the bare-metal machine (`analyze.py` there groups the failing points).
- **`explore.py --sweep freeze`.** A packet stream is (pair, direction, and either every packet with payload or one `freeze_match:` string in its own direction). For each stream and each swept step `s` (plus `s+1` as the boundary) it first runs `F=<pair>@s#0[:match]:1` and reads the guest's "freeze never fired: <N> of 0 matching events after step <s>" line, which hydo-init-freeze.sh counts in the helper's full log, so the console's 600-line trace limit does not matter. Step `s` holds N(s) − N(s+1) packets (+2 margin only where `s+1` is not swept; the last step N(s)), and the sweep runs one schedule `F=<svc><dir><peer>@<s>#<n>[:<match>]:<dur>` per packet. Options `--fc-pairs`, `--fc-dirs`, `--fc-steps`, `--fc-match all,manifest` (default), `--fc-durs` (default 150000), `--fc-margin`, `--sweep-every k`, `--sweep-with "<tokens>"` (one more fixed fault on every trace and point; a power cut is refused because its trace never reaches the count), `--sweep-dry` (trace and write `points.txt`), `--fc-traces` (reuse an earlier run's `fc-traces.jsonl`), and `--repro N` (re-runs per failure; default 2 for this sweep, 1 elsewhere, report key `repro_runs` only when ≠ 1). Point labels go to `sweep-points.jsonl`, so `compare.py sweep` tabulates them.
- **Redis control** (`explore-ob-redis-fc-disk.img`, `F=redis<workload`/`>`, all 20 steps, 3000 ms): 40 trace runs, 40 points, 40 freezes fired, 0 failures (the frozen step's SET times out and is not acknowledged), 186 s.
- **Benchmark d10/d11: not run.** `hvx/explore/stack-explore.sh` has no `F=`; the stack images carry neither `hydo_fc`, the pinned `iptables` nor the netfilter modules. Supporting it means porting `hydo-init-freeze.sh` into `stack-explore.sh` (parse `F=`, map mysql/kafka/redis/front to their ports and pid files, arm before an order, heal at the end, kill the helper at a cut), staging the three items in `build-stack.sh` as `hydo-build` does, and rebuilding the m59 `-pin-kr` control, d10 and d11 images — not small. By mechanism a freeze cannot trigger d11: d11 needs MySQL to keep serving reads while its FLUSHes stall, and a freeze stops the whole MySQL process; only the k-th-flush cut models it. d10 could be reachable as `F=kafka<front@s#n` (a produce held in flight) with `--sweep-with K=front@<s+1>+1`.
- **Not done:** the stack port above; a sweep combined with a power cut; the M73 open item (backward clock steps) is unchanged.

### Milestone 80 — DONE (the JavaScript/TypeScript assertion SDK for Node.js; a Node.js example on the Mac backend; 2026-10-24)

Branch `js-sdk` (not merged). No module or engine change.
- **The package** `sdk/js` (`hydo-assert`, `"private": true`, not published; no dependencies; CommonJS `index.js`, ESM `index.mjs` that re-exports it so both entries share one state; TypeScript types `index.d.ts`/`index.d.mts`, checked with `tsc` 6.0.3 under `node16` resolution from an `.mts` and a `.cts` file). API = the Go SDK's in camelCase: `always`, `alwaysOrUnreachable`, `sometimes`, `reachable`, `unreachable` with `check`/`hit`/`cmp` and the named comparison helpers `greaterThan`, `greaterThanOrEqualTo`, `lessThan`, `lessThanOrEqualTo`; `eventually(id, msg, withinMs)` with `begin`/`done`/`expire`, `awaitCond` (async) and `awaitCondSync` (blocks with `Atomics.wait`); `buggify(id, msg).fire(d)`; `catalog()`, `setupComplete()`; `emitLine(tag, value)` for other one-line record kinds. Records are written synchronously (`fs.writeSync`, one write per record) to `/dev/ttyS0`; `HYDO_ASSERT_OUT` = a path, `stderr` or `off` as in Go. Details are encoded as Go's `encoding/json` encodes the matching Go values (keys in UTF-8 byte order, HTML characters and U+2028/U+2029 escaped, Go's float format with `-0`, bigints as 64-bit integers, `Uint8Array` as base64, a lone surrogate as `�`; a NaN, an infinity or a cycle drops the record, as `json.Marshal` fails). BUGGIFY uses the Go configuration (`$HYDO_BUGGIFY`, else `/tmp/hydo-buggify`, parsed as Go parses it) and the same splitmix64/FNV-1a decisions in 64-bit `BigInt` arithmetic.

### Milestone 81 — DONE (Linux release runs without sudo; image builds independent of the time zone; the other seven 2-vCPU stack scenarios; 2026-10-24)

Branch `product-fixes` (from main `230ad15`). Three small fixes, each in its own commit. No module change; the main `/dev/hvx` and the bare-metal machine's live setup were not touched.
- **Runs without sudo in the Linux release** (`hvx/dist/hydo`, `libexec/hvx-run`, `install.sh`, `QUICKSTART-linux.md`, `README.md`). New `hydo module udev install|remove|status [--name N] [--group G] [--mode 0660] [--no-adduser] [--dry-run]`: `install` writes `/etc/udev/rules.d/70-hydo-N.rules` (`KERNEL=="N", SUBSYSTEM=="misc", GROUP="G", MODE="0660"`), creates the group (default `hydo`) if missing, adds the user, reloads udev and applies the rule to a loaded device; `remove` deletes the rule and sets the device back to root:root 0600. `install.sh --udev [--udev-group G] [--udev-name N]` runs `install` (sudo once); without `--udev` nothing changes. `libexec/hvx-run` drops the leading `sudo` when the user can read and write `$HVX_DEV` (default `/dev/hvx`; `HYDO_SUDO=1` keeps sudo) and passes `HVX_DEV` through sudo when it keeps it, so `hydo run` and `explore.py` both use sudo only when needed. `hydo` honours `HVX_DEV` (a side module, with its own lock file), uses `/var/tmp/hvx-snap-<uid>` when a run without sudo cannot write the root-made `/var/tmp/hvx-snap`, waits for udev after loading a module that has a rule, and `hydo doctor` / `module status` say who can open the device. Security meaning, stated in the rule file and the docs: anyone in the group can run guests through the kernel module, which was not hardened against hostile users, so the group is for people one would give sudo.
  **Checked on the bare-metal machine** with a release built from this branch (tarball `f01b1392…`, every asset matched `assets.sha256`) installed in `~/hydo-pf/prefix`, side module `hvxpf` (srcversion `CA5BF8BF2A0D66B312A68EF`, the main source), the login user's own group (so no group or membership was created): loaded first, `/dev/hvxpf` was `crw------- root root`; `install.sh --udev --udev-name hvxpf --udev-group <that group>` and `hydo module udev install` made it `crw-rw----` owned by root and that group (the trigger path), and an unload + load gave the new node the same (the add path); `hvx-run sudo id -u` printed 1000 on `/dev/hvxpf` and 0 on `/dev/hvx`. Then, as the login user with a `sudo` on PATH that only logs and fails: the Redis example image `8c828d3e…` (as in M75), `hydo run "disk=none | run"` OK `c513f10aee733aae` and `hydo run "disk=cut | run C=12 R=everysec"` VIOLATION k:2 `ecef6f8fe6c39ec0` (both the M75 values), `hydo explore --seeds 1-3 --strategy swarm --workers 1` (1 failure, lying-disk, reproduced and shrunk to `disk=lying:3 dseed=eac0b527c5ac67d9 | run C=20`, `715770dac37b9163`) and `hydo repro hydo-out/explore` (2 of 2 with the recorded fingerprint). The fake sudo was called 0 times; every sampled `hvx_explore` of these runs ran as the login user; snapshots went to `/var/tmp/hvx-snap-1000`. Afterwards `hydo module udev remove` gave `/dev/hvxpf` back to `root root 0600` (doctor then says runs use sudo), the side module was unloaded, and `/etc/udev/rules.d` is empty again; `/dev/hvx` stayed `crw------- root root` throughout.
- **Image builds independent of the time zone** (`hvx/onboard/hydo-build`, `hydo_oci.py`, `build-linux.sh`, `build-stack.sh`, `build-kafka.sh`, `build-mysql.sh`, `build-spread{,2,3}.sh`). libfaketime reads the frozen build time `2020-09-13 16:26:40` in the local zone, which is 1600000000 only in UTC+4 (the build machine's zone, UTC+4 all year). Every faketime'd call now gets `TZ=UTC-4` (POSIX for UTC+4; hydo-build's `FAKE_TZ`, `faketime_env()`), which on the build machine is the same instant. On the build machine, pinned tools, `hvx_seedrng` compiled with the pinned gcc (`c2a440c5…`; the `01adf1bd…` stand-in in `~/hydo/build` was not used), from main `230ad15` plus the fix: `examples/redis` gave `03beff6c…` (= `explore-ob-redis-nq-disk.img`) with no TZ, `TZ=UTC` and `TZ=America/New_York`; `examples/etcd` 3.6.15 gave `021d350a…` (= `explore-ob-etcd-3.6.15-nq-disk.img`) with no TZ, `TZ=UTC` and `TZ=Pacific/Auckland`; main without the fix gave the right Redis bytes with no TZ but `bfe8db2d…` under `TZ=UTC`. The hand-written scripts had the same dependency: `build-linux.sh`'s `mkext2_reproducible`, run from the script itself, gives the recorded `sql-disk.img` `b3b2b9c0…` and `redis-disk.img` `64c7e3f5…` in all three zones with the fix, and `c94536dd…`/`f96ed349…` (UTC) or `95384aa7…`/`0381d795…` (New York) without it. The other scripts were not rebuilt; their change is the same one-variable prefix on the same kind of call, and the pinned faketime gives 1600000000 both with no TZ and with `TZ=UTC-4` on the build machine (1600014400 under `TZ=UTC`). The release's wrapper already set `TZ=UTC-4` (M75) and is unchanged in effect.
- **The other seven stack fault scenarios on 2 vCPUs** (`HVX_VCPUS=2`, `stack-nq-disk.img`, harness from main in `~/hydo-pf`, byte-identical to M79's; full table in `hvx/REBASELINE.md` §7.6). Each `mode=fault` scenario two fresh runs plus a branch, all identical; the relaxed case `mode=sanity` twice, identical; all OK 30/30 exactly-once: kill mysql@10 `5787e8c2ab91c8dd`, kill kafka@20 `70f2262407cef26e`, kill redis@10 `124cc3dad8b93dfb` (27 cached), net mysql `c07c4bbbcde6d0d9` (first pass 29/30), net redis `962604a54396c17c`, net kafka `cbdbd77370547093` (first pass 28/30), net kafka with MySQL relaxed `51d0cedb269b4693` (first pass 22/30, 24/30 on 1 vCPU). No verdict differs in kind from 1 vCPU. With M79's Kafka kill at order 10, all eight scenarios now have 2-vCPU values.

Raw results: `/var/tmp/pf-smp/` (2-vCPU runs), `~/hydo-pf/sudoless/` and `~/hydo-pf/redis/hydo-out/` (sudo-less runs) on the bare-metal machine; the build machine build directory `~/hydo-pfb` was deleted after the builds.

### Milestone 82 — DONE (the Rust assertion SDK; a Rust example on both backends; 2026-10-24)

Branch `rust-sdk` (worktree `../hydo-rsdk`, main merged in after M81; not merged). No module or engine change.
- **The crate** `sdk/rust` (`hydo-assert`, `publish = false`, its own workspace, std only; features `noop` and `serde_json`). The Go SDK's run-time API in Rust names: `always`, `always_or_unreachable`, `sometimes`, `reachable`, `unreachable` (return `&'static Assertion`, registered at once), `check`/`hit`/`cmp` (any ordered value), `eventually(id, msg, within)` with `begin`/`done`/`expire`, `await_cond` (blocking) and `await_async` (takes a check future and a sleep future, so it works with tokio or any runtime), `buggify(id, msg).fire(d)`, `catalog()`, `setup_complete()`, and `emit_line(tag, value)` for other one-line record kinds. Rust additions: call-site macros that capture file and line (`hydo_always!(cond, "id" => "msg", {"k": v})`, without an id the message is the id; `hydo_sometimes!`, `hydo_reachable!`, `hydo_unreachable!`, `hydo_always_or_unreachable!`, `hydo_always_cmp!`/`hydo_sometimes_cmp!` and the named `hydo_{always,sometimes}_{greater_than,greater_than_or_equal_to,less_than,less_than_or_equal_to}!`, `hydo_buggify!`, `hydo_eventually!`) and `declare!` for named statics. Both register before `main` with a std-only constructor (`.init_array` on ELF, `__mod_init_func` on Mach-O, lock-free intrusive list, no allocation), so properties in code that never runs are in the catalog; macro records carry one more field, `"loc":"<file>:<line>"`, last. Catalog order: `declare!` entries and macro sites sorted by file, line, column (a `declare!` block in the order written), then run-time declarations in declaration order. Details: `details!{..}` / `Details` (a `BTreeMap`, bytewise key order), encoded as Go's `encoding/json` encodes them (HTML characters and U+2028/U+2029 escaped, Go's float forms such as `1e+21` and `1.5e-7`, `f32` as Go's `float32`; a NaN or an infinity drops the record). Output, deduplication and BUGGIFY configuration and decisions are the Go SDK's.
- **Byte-for-byte proof** (`sdk/rust/tests/conformance.sh`): a Go program built against `hvx/stack/hydoassert`'s own sources and `examples/conformance.rs` make the same calls (every type, dedup, comparisons with an unknown operator, NaN/Inf records, eventually, 8 fault points × 50 rounds, details with nested maps and lists, uint64/int64 extremes, floats at the formatting boundaries, f32, control and HTML characters, U+2028/U+2029). Three BUGGIFY configurations (seed in the environment, in the file, none): consoles and stdouts identical with Go 1.26.5 and with Go 1.27.3 (console sha256 prefixes `3cc3f8d11d37a639` / `3d3e4ea08c555c4e` / `09906536cadbbe64`). `cargo test` (also `--features noop` and `--features serde_json`): encoder, BUGGIFY parse rules and rates over 400 seeds, the macros, catalog order and `loc`, `await_async` under tokio, `emit_line`.
- **Example `hvx/onboard/examples/rust-kv`:** `rkv`, a key/value server over TCP on loopback with an append-only log, plus its client and oracle (`serve`, `put`, `ping`, `check`): `always` (acked PUT durable; log size via a comparison macro), `always_or_unreachable` (log lines parse), `sometimes` (recovered, PUT without reply, oracle had to ask again), `reachable` (torn tail), `eventually` (serves within 5 s), three BUGGIFY points; knob `S=never` turns off fdatasync; the oracle writes the catalog (the server starts before S1, so its records then are not in a run's console). `build-rkv.sh [aarch64]` links a static musl binary with rust-lld (Rust 1.90.0, no C toolchain); two clean builds identical (x86_64 `a26ef466…`, arm64 `e5d97b55…`). `hydo-build` gains nothing new for it beyond the M80-merged `buggify: true`.
- **Mac backend** (bare-metal machine crowded; Mac release 0.1.0 installed into a scratch prefix with this branch's `hydo-build`, `hydo-init-buggify.sh` and `manifest_space.py` copied in): image `explore-ob-rust-kv-arm64` (cpio `500ecb2f…`, disk `e19be506…`), two builds identical. Each schedule twice, identical: `disk=none | run` OK acked=20 `64de839903b96e45`; `disk=cut | run C=12` OK acked=12 `6a7e5947973e5770`; `disk=cut | run C=12 S=never` VIOLATION acked=12 lost=12 `6f29e36a1cd516be`; `K=rkv@8+2` OK `375ca29fb8f1ab23`; `B=5abc,1000,500` OK acked=2 `de31ab2024fb243f`; `B=1234` OK `244342f8f8aaa1e9`; `K=rkv@8+2 B=1234` OK `0be47ac30f845cb6`; `P=rkv@5+3` OK `d45afcdc04b39994`. `hydo_assert_report` over the 20 consoles lists all 13 rkv properties (`rkv.acked_durable` FAIL from the `S=never` cut, `rkv.torn_tail` NOT EXERCISED). `hydo explore --seeds 1-16 --strategy swarm --buggify --workers 2` twice: all 16 schedules carry `B=`, same 16 fingerprints, same property table; 8 failures, all reproduced, all lying disk / relaxed `S` / I/O errors; the three fault points fired (6, 4, 1). ### Milestone 83 — DONE (the Python assertion SDK; a Python example on the Mac backend; 2026-10-24)

Branch `python-sdk` (worktree `../hydo-pysdk`, main merged in after M82; not merged). No module or engine change.
- **The package** `sdk/python` (distribution `hydo-assert`, import `hydo_assert`, version 0.1.0, `pyproject.toml` with the classifier `Private :: Do Not Upload`; standard library only; Python 3.8+; not published). The Go SDK's API in Python's names: `always`, `always_or_unreachable`, `sometimes`, `reachable`, `unreachable` (return an `Assertion`, declared at module level so the catalog is complete at import), `check`/`hit`/`cmp` and the named comparison helpers `greater_than`, `greater_than_or_equal_to`, `less_than`, `less_than_or_equal_to`; `eventually(id, msg, within_seconds)` with `begin`/`done`/`expire`, blocking `await_cond(cond, poll)` and `await await_async(cond, poll)` for asyncio (a plain or `async` condition); `buggify(id, msg)` with `fire(details)`; `catalog()`, `setup_complete()`, `emit_line(tag, value)`. One reentrant process-wide lock, never held across a blocking call or an `await`; fresh locks after `fork`. `HYDO_ASSERT_OUT=<path>|stderr|off` as in Go, plus `logging` (Python's logger `hydo_assert`). The caller's details dict is copied, never changed.
- **Encoder:** writes what Go's `encoding/json` writes: keys in UTF-8 byte order, Go's escapes (`<>&`, U+2028/2029, `\b`/`\f`, `\u00xx`), Go's float format (`1e+21`, `1.5e-7`, `3`, `-0`), a NaN or infinity drops the record (still counted as written, as in Go). Python-only types: tuples as arrays, `bytes` as base64 (Go's `[]byte`), sets as sorted arrays, other objects as `str()`. A lone surrogate is `�`, as Go 1.26 writes an invalid UTF-8 byte (Go 1.27 writes a raw U+FFFD; the guest Go is 1.26.5).
- **Byte-for-byte proof** (`sdk/python/tests/conformance.sh`, pins `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.5` as `sdk/js` does): a Go program built against `hvx/stack/hydoassert`'s own sources and `tests/conformance.py` make the same calls (every type, dedup, all comparison helpers incl. an unknown operator, NaN/Inf, eventually, 9 fault points × 60 rounds, details with nested maps and lists, int64/uint64 extremes, floats at the format boundaries, `[]byte`, HTML and control characters, emoji, CJK, invalid UTF-8, unicode keys and ids) under eight BUGGIFY configurations (seed in the environment, in the file, none, and five malformed or edge configurations that Go's `strconv` must reject or accept: `  BEEF,07,+5\t`, `0xbeef`, a 65-bit seed, `ab, 300,1_0`, all points always firing). Consoles and stdouts identical with Go 1.26.5 + Python 3.15.0 and 3.8.20 (Mac), Go 1.26.5 + CPython 3.11.9 (build machine), and Go 1.27.3 (invalid-UTF-8 case skipped). `python3 -m unittest discover -s sdk/python/tests`: 14 tests (encoder, dedup, NaN, catalog order, 16 threads × 2000 evaluations with no interleaved line, asyncio eventually, fork, BUGGIFY determinism and rates) pass on 3.8.20 and 3.15.0. `pip install ./sdk/python` into a Python 3.8 virtualenv works.
- **Example `hvx/onboard/examples/python-kv`** (Mac backend; the bare-metal machine was crowded): `pykv.py`, an asyncio TCP key/value server with an append-only log, plus its client and oracle; properties `always` (acked PUT durable; log size via `less_than_or_equal_to`), `always_or_unreachable` (log lines parse), `sometimes` (non-empty log replayed, PUT without a reply), `reachable` (torn tail), `unreachable` (unknown command), `eventually` (the server answers within 5 s of the oracle's start), two BUGGIFY points (lost reply, slow PUT). Python is the pinned aarch64 CPython 3.11.9 (`ic0l2ykss28lr7r4by14inb3pqw87yza`), staged by `fetch-python-arm64.sh` (1317 files, 52 MB, `files.sha256`); manifest `hydo-mac.yaml` with `buggify: true` and knob `S` (fsync). Image `explore-ob-python-kv-arm64` (cpio `d96a0feb…`, disk `93c5d2ca…`), two builds identical, built with the rebuilt Mac release 0.1.0 (2026-10-24) in a scratch prefix.
- **Results** (each schedule twice, identical; `RESULTS.md`): `disk=none | run` OK acked=20 `bfe5a4e04ca43a71`; `K=pykv@8+2` OK acked=18 `3c05e0fa3796cea2`; `disk=cut | run C=12` OK `4f40677ee1ce1be2`; `disk=cut | run C=12 S=never` VIOLATION `key k:0 lost` `74debdd69ee7af08`; `B=5abc,1000,500` OK, both points fire `092c90dc4c56d181`; `K=pykv@5+2 B=77,1000,300` OK `0b1d382236c21141`. `hydo_assert_report` gives the same table for both runs of each schedule and exits 1 only for the `S=never` cut. `hydo explore --seeds 1-20 --strategy swarm --workers 2 --buggify`, twice: same 20 schedules, fingerprints, verdicts and report; 10 failures, all reproduced, all expected (6 lying disk, 3 `S=never` with a cut, 1 injected I/O errors); minimal `disk=lying:3 dseed=eac0b527c5ac67d9 | run C=20` (`1d1caf745e0ee594`) and `disk=cut dseed=dd8d1ecadadb959b | run C=9 S=never` (`f963db2572fe465d`); the report's property table lists the program's own properties (`kv.acked_durable` 13 ok / 9 fail, `kv.back` 19 in time, both BUGGIFY points fired; `kv.torn_tail` never exercised).
- **Found on the way:** `manifest_space.restrict` dropped the `B=` token for manifest projects, so `--buggify` was silently inert there; fixed the same way on main by M80 (the merged fix is used here). A manifest knob named `B` is refused by `manifest_space` (reserved token), so `buggify: true` is the only way to feed the SDKs' seed.
