### Milestone 142 — DONE (the schedule is parsed once, and the hvx engine is called with Rust values instead of text inside the process; every recorded answer and every bare-metal and Mac check identical before and after; 2026-11-02)

Branch `worktree-agent-af02eaa9cab9cd779` (from `main` = `3a9986e`), with one part done by a second agent on `worktree-agent-adeac7c4af223704b` (merged). Decided by the user: "a good core, good structure, so I can extend it without thinking about what's inconsistent". Bare-metal machine tree `~/hydo-m142` (and `~/hydo-m142-before` at `3a9986e`), scripts `~/hydo-m142-work/` (`build.sh`, `explore.sh`, `checks.sh`, `boxchk.sh`), results `/var/tmp/m142`; at most two VMs, every VM through `~/bin/hvx-run`; the main module (`B5E97B37504F1A5F508BA30`) was not reloaded, `hvx.c`/`hvx_abi.h` and `hv/hvm/` were not touched.

- **Before, a schedule was read three times.** `hydo-schedule` parsed it for the explorer and the CLI; the hvx engine (`hydo-hvx/src/sched.rs`, the C engine's `parse_sched` ported in M132) parsed its text again with `strstr` and `strtoull`; and `hydo-control` printed the typed guest tokens back to text and took them apart with `split`/`split_once`. **Now `hydo-schedule` is the only reader.** `hydo_hvx::sched::Sched::from_schedule(&Schedule)` computes the values the engine arms (disk fault class and probability, tick jitter with its defaults, `pp=`/`xt*`, `q=`/`qs=`/`qb=`/`qbs=`/`qm=`, `rb=`, `cf=`/`cfn`, the power cut from a `C=` token) and the guest text it types; `hydo-control` acts on `GuestToken` values (N=/O= as target, window and `Netem` list; F= as `Freeze`; H= as `ProtocolFault`; W= as `Compose`; knobs as tokens; the cadence as `HostToken::Rb`). How to add a token is written in `hydo-schedule/src/lib.rs` ("The one parser, and how to add a token").
- **Every parser difference, resolved.** The C parser's port moved to the test model `hydo-hvx/tests/c_model/`; `tests/parse_vs_c.rs` checks that the model still gives the recorded C answers (`tests/golden/parse_sched_c.txt`, unchanged: 23,351 inputs, 3,971 refused) and then compares the engine's new path with it on every input. On the 9,286 inputs both accept, the engine arms exactly what the C armed (every field; the host text itself is no longer kept, because nothing used it). No input the C refused is accepted. 10,094 inputs the C engine ran are refused by hydo-schedule; their classes, with counts and one example each, are recorded in `tests/golden/parse_differences.txt`: a host token twice (the C read the first one, 1,753), a host word that is not a known `key=value` (the C ignored it, 1,183), a host value that is not a whole number in range or not its form (the C read a number prefix, a wrapped number or 0; per key, 1,390 in all), a modifier without its main token or `tjx=` with `tj=` (the C ignored it, 157), a guest part not in its one layout (one space after `|`, then `run`, one space between tokens; 1,504), a guest word that is not `<LETTER>=<value>` (1,750), a guest token its grammar refuses (per letter, 2,351 in all), and a guest part longer than 511 bytes (the C cut it, 6). The decision for all of them: refuse. No input of these classes can reach the engine from hydo itself (the explorer, `hydo run`/`repro`, the controller and hydo-bench all hand it a parsed `Schedule`, printed canonically); only a person typing to the program `hydo-hvx` can send one, and the program now answers it as the C answered a schedule it could not read (`RESULT ? fp=0 wfp=0 secs=0 verdict=ERROR bad request`, `BRANCHEND ? bad request`, or `hvx_explore: bad schedule` and exit status 2 for `one`). The boot schedule of `--control boot serve` may be left out (it was `|`, which hydo-schedule refuses; leaving it out is the same empty schedule). In `hydo-control`, the paths only a non-canonical token could reach are gone (the "bad freeze token" and "bad one-way direction" verdicts, the composer's unknown-field lines and its crash path); delay text with jitter or `us`/`s` units, which the old N=/O= reader handled, cannot be written in a schedule.
- **Before, the in-process engine was called with text.** The hvx engine thread exchanged the old protocol's lines (CTL, RESUME, SEND, STOP, SNAP, CONT, END, DISKOFF, CUT, RESULT, …) with hydo-engine over in-process pipes and was configured with a command line. **Now the calls are Rust values.** The new crate `hydo/crates/hydo-engine-proto` holds them: `Request` (Run, Ctl, Resume, Branch, Quit), `HostCmd` (Send, Ack, Snap, DiskOff, Cut, Cont, End), `Answer` (Send, Ack, Snap, DiskOff, Cut, Refused), `EngineMsg` (Ready, Event, Sent, Drop, Stop, Answer, Result, BranchPoint, BranchEnd, Other), `RunResult`, `Ready`, `BranchRequest`, each with its one line (`line()`, `parse()`); hydo-engine re-exports them where they were (`protocol`, `lockstep`). The host's end is `hydo_engine::link::Link` with two implementations: `ChanLink` (channels to an engine thread of this process) and `TextLink` (an engine program's stdin and stdout). The engine's end is `hydo_hvx::port::Port`: `ChanPort` in process and `hydo_hvx::text::TextPort` for the program `hydo-hvx`, which reads the host's lines with the C engine's own leniency (`fgets` pieces of 4,095 bytes, a NUL ends a line, `sscanf` words, `strtoull` numbers) and prints every value's line. The engine is configured with `hydo_hvx::engine::Start` (mode, control, paths, RAM, vCPUs, CPU level) and run by `engine::run`; `engine::main_with` is now the program's command-line reader in front of it. The worker, the lock-step client (`Lockstep` over a `Link`), the controller's link and the explorer's workers use the values; a transcript (`with_log`) writes each value's line, or the line an engine program printed. The Mac engine `hvmx` keeps its text protocol and is driven through `TextLink` (its lines and hvx's are the same text); M143's Rust port of it can implement `Port` directly. How to add an engine request, command or report is written in `hydo-engine-proto/src/lib.rs` ("Adding to the protocol").
- **What can differ, and only on input hydo never sends:** a RESULT whose verdict ends in spaces is printed without them by the program (the value is the one `RunResult::parse` reads, which trims); an `OK snap` answer whose retype list was cut at 512 bytes (`,...`) is no longer read as an answer (it was a protocol error before too, with other words); error messages for a malformed engine line name the value instead of the old enum. For a bad schedule given to the program together with an unreadable file, the program now names the schedule first.
- **Proof without a VM.** `cargo test --locked --release --workspace` on the Mac: 343 tests passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored (105 test binaries); every recorded answer unchanged (no golden re-blessed except the new `parse_differences.txt`); `hydo-control`'s corpus tests (corpus, corpus_net, features, fakes, m123: the same 60 tests as before the change) pass with typed tokens; `hydo-engine/tests/lockstep.rs` now replays every recorded lock-step transcript of both engines twice, over the text link and over the channel link, and checks that every engine line is a value that prints back byte for byte and that the client's own transcript is the recorded one; `hydo-engine-proto`'s round-trip tests; `hydo-hvx`'s `text` tests (the C engine's lenient reading). `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean on the Mac, and clippy is clean for `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` on hydo-hvx, hydo-engine, hydo-engine-proto and hydo-control (the engine itself compiles only on Linux).
- **Proof on the bare-metal machine** (tree at `93f40f4`; the commits after it change formatting, a lint attribute and documents only): `hv/hvx/deploy-metal.sh` ALL PASS (33 checks), the pinned reproducers through the program `hydo-hvx` (the text path) `2403499c9a3f8419` and `f87130453609a5d6`, and again from both trees with `checks.sh`; `hv/hvx/lockstep-metal.sh check` ALL PASS (18 groups, every value the recorded one); M121's `agent_boot_check` on the M140 Redis agent image from both trees: ALL PASS with the same values (boot and S0 `cac12297e6c6231c`, S1 runs and fresh boots `c4ef80ee8733f9f1`, `stops=22366 typed=14 inh=fedc980c50b0c589`); four explorations with `explore.sh` (pool of 2, in-process engine, the host-call port on as by default), each identical by `engine_equiv` to the same exploration from `~/hydo-m142-before` (which was itself run twice and was identical to itself): Redis swarm seeds 1–40 (69 runs, 20 failures shrunk, 108 consoles), Redis process with `--more-faults` seeds 1–40 (41 runs with 8 `C=` and 7 `cf=` power cuts, 56 consoles), the adaptive freeze sweep on redis-freeze (80 runs), and the stack-explore image `explore-disk.img` seeds 1–10 with shrinking (21 runs, 30 consoles); and the Redis swarm exploration again with in-place reuse (`HYDO_HVX_REUSE=1`, M138) identical to the before tree's fresh-VM exploration (69 runs, 108 consoles).
- **Proof on the Mac** (main `3a9986e` built in a scratch copy against this branch; both with their own `hvmx` from the unchanged `hv/hvm/explore`): `hv/hvm/explore/lockstep-check.sh`'s `check` group (M116's timed-input, reaction and mid-run branch experiment on `explore-ob-redis-oci-arm64`) gives the same 14 lines, each the recorded value, from both builds; its `run` group stops with `NotReady("")` from both builds, because the only Redis arm64 image on this Mac is an agent image (every image is one since M136) and the group boots it as a plain serve worker (the script predates M136); and a Redis swarm exploration on hvm (`--seeds 1-12 --strategy swarm --workers 2`, an M140 agent image) is identical by `engine_equiv` (27 runs, 6 failures shrunk to 4 minimal schedules, 46 consoles); the only differences it prints are the `repro_command` texts, which name each tree's own `hvmx` path.
- **Left:** `hv/hvm/explore/lockstep-check.sh`'s `run` group needs a shell image or an agent-image variant (it was not touched: `hv/hvm/` belongs to M143); the Mac engine still parses its schedule's host part in C (`serve.c`) until M143 ports it, so a host token for the Mac is added in two places until then; `hydo-control` prints a token's value text with a private helper (`token_value`), where a public `GuestToken` accessor in hydo-schedule would be cleaner; a few engine-internal names stay text (`Ctl.phase`, the `tjinfo` extras text whose 160-byte cut the RESULT keeps), turned into values at the boundary.

### Milestone 144 — DONE (one typed configuration, read in one place: every environment variable in one inventory, read once at a program's start and passed down; nothing user-visible moved; 2026-11-02)

Branch `worktree-agent-a35ac4ca583bd8092` (from `main` = `c5f8ff1`). Decided by the user: a consistent core that is easy to extend. Bare-metal machine tree `~/hydo-m144`, scripts `~/hydo-m144-work/` (`build.sh`, `explore.sh`, `all.sh`), results `/var/tmp/m144`; at most two VMs, every VM through `~/bin/hvx-run`; the main module (`B5E97B37504F1A5F508BA30`) was not reloaded, `hvx.c`/`hvx_abi.h` and `hv/hvm/` were not touched.

- **Before,** about 113 distinct `HYDO_*`/`HVX_*` names were read across the crates, each where it was needed (`std::env::var` in hydo-engine, hydo-hvx, hydo-explore's pool, hydo-build's tool lookups, hydo-manifest's version check, hydo-control's rewind switch, hydo-bench, hydo-grpc-gen, hydo-nix-fetch), and the `hydo` command passed values to the explorer and to hydo-build by setting variables in its own process (`set_var` of the release's paths, the lock, `HYDO_HVX_EXPLORE`, every build input). Nobody could see what could be configured.
- **The inventory** is `hydo/crates/hydo-config/src/registry.rs` (a `variables!` list: name, owner group, kind, type, default, readers, documentation; each entry is also a constant of its name), printed as `hydo/crates/hydo-config/INVENTORY.md`. Counts: 36 user-facing and 44 developer-only variables (diagnostics, a tree's paths, checks) are read from hydo's environment; 32 test switches are read by test code only (`HYDO_BLESS`, `HYDO_RELEASE_SCHEMA`, the corpus and recording switches; they stay in the tests); 24 names are the guest interface (set by the controller for guest commands, or read by the guest programs hydo-agent, hydo-world, hydo-grpc, hydo-read, whose bytes are pinned and so were not changed); 4 are variables of an image's manifest.sh the host reads back; 2 are set for the hvm program (`HVM_DISK`, `HVM_DISK_OUT`). **Removed (5):** `HYDO_SNAP_DIR`, `HVX_SNAP_DIR`, `HVX_SNAP_MALLOC`, `HYDO_SNAPSHOTS` (the deleted C engine's snapshot files; hydo-hvx keeps snapshots in memory and never read them; `HYDO_SNAPSHOTS` changed only the pool's printed line) and `HYDO_CLI` (told the explorer program that the deleted Python CLIs started it). Shell scripts and the C programs keep their own variables (not in the inventory).
- **One place to read, typed groups passed down.** `hydo_config::Env::process()` reads the registered variables (and `HOME` for defaults) once; `hydo_config::Config` holds the typed groups: `engine::Engine` (choice, sudo, device, lock, program), `hvx::Options` (the hvx engine's options; hydo-hvx re-exports it as `engine::Options`, moved there from hydo-hvx), `run::Paths` (root, build directory, wrapper), `run::Pool` (quiet file, cache), `run::Bench`, `run::Control` (`HVM_SPIN_REWIND`), `run::Cli` (`HYDO_CLI_PLATFORM`), `build::Build` (every build input as an `Input` that carries its variable's name for hydo-build's messages, `HYDO_AGENT_UNPINNED`, `HYDO_KEEP_OWNERS`, `HYDO_VERSION_CHECK`) and `tools::Tools`. The programs' `main`s read it: `hydo` (`Ctx::new(Config::process())`), `hydo-build`, `hydo-hvx`, `hydo-explore`, `hydo-bench`, `hydo-grpc-gen`, `hydo-nix-fetch`, and the engine examples. It is passed down explicitly: `hydo_engine::hvx::Hvx` gained `config` (the values; for an engine in this process its options are read from them with `env` and `extra_env` on top), `hvx::program(root, &Engine)`, `hvx::wrapper_env(&Engine)` (the lock, device and sudo the wrapper and the engine program get), `hydo_explore::Env.config`, `pool::Host.pool`, `hydo_bench::main_with(argv, root, &Config)`, `hydo_build::Ctx.inputs` (`Ctx::standalone(inputs)`), `hydo_manifest::LoadOptions.version_check_warn`, `AgentEngine::with_control`, `hydo_grpc_gen::main_with(argv, &Tools)`. The `hydo` command no longer sets any hydo variable in its own environment: `hydo build` fills the release's paths into a copy of `config.build`, `hydo explore` gives the explorer `hvxenv::explore_config` (the release's `guest/`, `libexec/hvx-run`, lock file and engine program); only `PATH` is still prepended for the tools the engine wrapper starts.
- **No configuration file,** on purpose (`hydo-config/src/lib.rs`): what a project tests lives in its versioned files and schedules; what is left is per machine (the release fills in its own paths), per exploration (a shared bare-metal machine's quiet window or cache) or a developer diagnostic for one run, and a file would add a second place and a precedence rule for no option anyone sets once and keeps. "How to add an option" is in the same file.
- **Tests** (`hydo/crates/hydo-config/tests/inventory.rs`): `INVENTORY.md` must be the printed inventory (`HYDO_BLESS=1` rewrites it); no workspace crate other than hydo-config (and the pinned guest programs) calls `env::var`/`var_os`/`set_var`/`remove_var` with a hydo name or with a non-literal name (two system-variable readers are listed with their reason), and `Env::process()`/`Config::process()` appear only in a program's `main`; every exact hydo name literal in a crate's code, and every name a test or example reads or sets, is in the inventory, and every entry is used (a host variable by a typed group of hydo-config); the removed names appear nowhere. Checked by planting a read of `HYDO_FOO` in hydo-history: two tests failed and named the line.
- **What changed at the edges, never in a result:** `HVX_DEV` set to an empty value now means `/dev/hvx` everywhere (the in-process choice and the engine read it as the device "" before; the CLI already treated it as unset); the engine program's command line under the wrapper no longer carries `HVX_SNAP_DIR=… [HVX_SNAP_MALLOC=1]` (so the `repro_command` text of hvx runs is shorter); `hydo doctor` no longer checks a snapshot directory nobody writes; the explorer's pool line says "in memory" whenever the snapshots fit (it said what `HYDO_SNAPSHOTS` asked); the program `hydo-explore` always writes the "by hand" lines of a tree (only `hydo explore` names `hydo run`).
- **For M143 (the Rust Mac runner, in parallel):** its program reads hvm's options through hydo-config: add a group (for example `hydo_config::hvm::Options`) with a field per `HVM_*`/`HVMX_*` variable `serve.c`/`hvm.c` read, register each in `registry.rs` (kind user or developer), call `Env::process()` in the program's `main`, and pass the options to the engine (the in-process path takes them from `Hvm`'s configuration, as `Hvx.config`). `HVM_SPIN_REWIND` is already the host controller's (`run::Control`); `HVM_DISK`/`HVM_DISK_OUT` are listed as names set for the program. The inventory test fails on any `std::env::var("HVM_…")` in the new crate.
- **Proof without a VM.** `cargo test --locked --release --workspace` on the Mac: 350 tests passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored (108 test binaries); no golden was re-blessed (the only new recorded file is `INVENTORY.md`). `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean on the Mac; clippy is clean for `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` on hydo-hvx, hydo-engine, hydo-control and hydo-config from the Mac, and on the bare-metal machine (Linux) for hydo-cli, hydo-explore, hydo-bench, hydo-engine, hydo-hvx and hydo-config.
- **Proof on the bare-metal machine** (tree `~/hydo-m144` at `c7bd258`, module `B5E97B37504F1A5F508BA30`): `HVX_METAL_TREE=hydo-m144 hv/hvx/deploy-metal.sh` ALL PASS (33 checks, the pinned reproducers among them: `2403499c9a3f8419` VIOLATION order 11 and `f87130453609a5d6` OK, also again through the program `hydo-hvx`); `hv/hvx/lockstep-metal.sh check` ALL PASS (every value the recorded one); M121's `agent_boot_check` ALL PASS with M142's values (S0 `cac12297e6c6231c`, S1 runs and fresh boots `c4ef80ee8733f9f1`, `stops=22366 typed=14 inh=fedc980c50b0c589`). Explorations compared by `engine_equiv` with main's records (M142's `/var/tmp/m142/after*`, made by the M142 tree, whose code is main's, on the same module and images): the Redis swarm exploration seeds 1–40 (69 runs, 108 consoles) and the process exploration with `--more-faults` seeds 1–40 (41 runs with power cuts and k-th-flush cuts, 56 consoles), both IDENTICAL. **Every override still works:** `HYDO_HVX_REUSE=1` (reuse in place) gives main's reuse record (69 runs, 108 consoles, IDENTICAL); `HYDO_HVX_HOSTCALL=0` (port off) gives exactly what main's tree gives with the same setting (seeds 1–12, 27 runs, 45 consoles, IDENTICAL), and the setting is read (seed 1's fingerprint is `298b4df666392c81` with the port off and `665d0826891a4769` with it on, as the transport changes the guest's timing); `HYDO_ENGINE=process` with `HYDO_HVX_EXPLORE` started the program (two `hydo-hvx` processes seen while it ran) and gives the in-process exploration (seeds 1–12, 26 runs, 44 consoles, IDENTICAL); run as the normal user, the default picks the program through `hvx-run sudo` (IDENTICAL again), and `HYDO_ENGINE=inproc` forces the engine into the explorer's own process, which then fails with "open /dev/hvx: Permission denied" as it must. Results in `/var/tmp/m144` (`all.log`).
- **Proof on the Mac:** a Redis swarm exploration on hvm (`--seeds 1-12 --strategy swarm --workers 2`, the M140 agent image of M142's proof) with main `c5f8ff1` built in a scratch copy and with this branch, both with the same `hvmx`: identical by `engine_equiv` (27 runs, 6 failures shrunk to 4 minimal schedules, 46 consoles); the only differences printed are the four `repro_command` texts, which name each tree's own `hvmx` path.
- **Left:** `BootSpec::snapshots` / `SnapshotStore` no longer change anything for hvx (hydo-hvx keeps its snapshots in memory) and could be removed with the pool line's word; the `Config`'s raw values (`Config::env`) and its typed `engine` group are two views of one thing, joined only by `hvx::wrapper_env` where the `hydo` command changes the typed group (the release's lock file); the guest programs (hydo-agent, hydo-world, hydo-grpc, hydo-read) still read their own variables directly, because their bytes are pinned; shell scripts and the C programs (`hv/`, `hydo/dist/`) keep their own variables, outside the inventory; the Mac engine's variables (`HVM_*` read by `serve.c`/`hvm.c`) join the inventory with M143.

### Milestone 143 — DONE (the Mac run engine in Rust, `hydo/crates/hydo-hvm`: `hv/hvm/hvm.c`, the virtio devices, the spin observer and `hv/hvm/explore/serve.c` (hvmx) ported function by function on Hypervisor.framework, on M142's typed calls and M144's typed configuration; the program `hydo-hvm` is the Mac default, `HYDO_HVM=c` runs the C hvmx for one milestone, `HYDO_HVM=inproc` runs the engine in the calling process; every comparison identical to the C engine; 2026-11-02)

Branch `worktree-agent-a78484ce5b2e946c3` (from `main` = `3a9986e`; main's M142 `c5f8ff1` and M144 `a6abac8` merged in). No change to `hv/hvm/*.c`. Mac only (an M2 Pro shared with another session's VMs; at most two VMs of this work at a time); the bare-metal machine and the build machine were not used.

- **The crate.** `hv.rs`: Hypervisor.framework through FFI (the VM, the vCPU, registers, system and SIMD registers, the stage-2 protection, the pending IRQ, debug traps, `hv_vcpus_exit`, the instruction-cache flush); the SIMD register write passes its 16-byte vector in `q0` from inline assembly, because stable Rust cannot pass a vector by value through FFI. `mem.rs`: guest RAM (anonymous, locked unless `HVMX_NO_MLOCK`) and the snapshot buffers (an unlinked file in `HVM_SNAP_DIR`, as the C kept them). These two files hold all of the crate's `unsafe`. `layout.rs`, `machine.rs` (`struct mach` with its C byte layout for the fingerprints, the GIC, the UART, tick jitter and PCT points), `fdt.rs` (the device tree), `virtio.rs` (the transport, the block device with hvx's seeded faults and the volatile write cache, the network device), `vmm.rs` (hvm.c: the run loop and its interrupt delivery rule, the exit handlers, the vCPU snapshot, the watchdog, both fingerprints), `spin.rs` (spin_observer.c: exact-repeat loops, counter loops and the rewind mode's copy-on-write checkpoint), `serve.rs` (serve.c: S0/S1, RUN, CTL, RESUME, the lock-step protocol, the controlled boot of agent images, DISKOFF/CUT, the power cut's recovery boot, the automatic rewind re-run, `HVMX_DIAG`, `HVMX_CHECK_RESTORE`) and `hvm_main.rs` (hvm.c's own `run`/`print`/`branch`). Every function keeps its C name and order of effects; the C engine's stderr lines keep their words (`hvmx: ...`, `hvm: SPIN: ...`), so `hydo run`'s filters see the same lines.
- **Typed, with the text at the boundary (M142).** The engine core takes `hydo_engine_proto` values through `hydo_hvx::port::Port` and emits `EngineMsg` values; every schedule is a `hydo_schedule::Schedule` (the C engine's host-part parser is not ported: the host tokens are read from the typed `HostToken`s; `rb=`, `spin=rewind`, `pct*`, `tj*`, `disk=`/`dseed=` as hvmx applied them, the hvx-only tokens refused with hvmx's words). The program reads hvmx's request lines with `hydo_hvx::text::TextPort`, the reader of hvx's program, which reads them with the C engines' leniency; the in-process engine talks over `ChanPort`/`ChanLink`. As on hvx, a schedule hydo-schedule refuses is answered `RESULT ? ... verdict=ERROR bad request` where hvmx read it loosely, and the guest part typed is the canonical guest text (hydo-schedule requires the one space after `|` the Mac engine typed).
- **Configuration (M144).** `hydo-config/src/hvm.rs`: `hvm::Engine` (`HYDO_HVM`, `HYDO_HVM_ENGINE`, read by hydo-engine) and `hvm::Options` (every `HVM_*`/`HVMX_*` variable hvm.c, virtio.c and serve.c read), registered in `registry.rs` (group `Hvm`; `HVM_DISK`/`HVM_DISK_OUT` are now read by hydo-hvm, so they moved from "set for programs" to the group); `INVENTORY.md` regenerated. `hydo-hvm`'s `main` reads them once; the in-process engine takes them from `Hvm.config` with `Hvm.env` and the image's `HVM_DISK` on top.
- **The default and the switches** (`hydo-engine/src/hvm.rs`). `hvm::program(root, &config.hvm)`: `HYDO_HVM_ENGINE`; else with `HYDO_HVM=c` the C `hv/hvm/explore/hvmx`; else a tree's `target/release/hydo-hvm` or a release's `bin/hydo-hvm`; else (a release built before M143) hvmx. A `hydo-hvm` without the hypervisor entitlement is signed ad hoc before it runs (`ensure_signed`; cargo builds it unsigned). `HYDO_HVM=inproc` (`hydo-engine/src/hvm_inproc.rs`) runs the engine on a thread of the calling process: Hypervisor.framework gives a process one VM, so it serves one engine at a time (a second ends with a message naming the limit) and the calling program itself must carry the entitlement; it is meant for `hydo run` and checks, not for a pool of workers. The explorer, `hydo run`/`repro`, `hydo doctor` (checks the engine it will run and its signature) and the examples take the engine from `program`. The Mac release script builds and ships `bin/hydo-hvm` (still with the C `hvm`/`hvmx`) and `install.sh` signs it; the release was not rebuilt. `hv/hvm/explore/lockstep-check.sh` tests `hydo-hvm` (`ENGINE=c`: hvmx) and has an agent-image variant of its `run` and `rewind` groups (M142 found the old `run` group stopping with NotReady on agent-only images): `hydo-control/examples/hvm_agent_check.rs` drives each schedule through the host controller from the host's S1 twice and from a fresh boot twice and requires one fingerprint, one `ctl=` and one verdict.
- **Proofs.** `tests/c_layout.rs` compiles hvm.c and virtio.c with a probe (`tests/probe.c`) and checks every Hypervisor.framework constant the port names, the snapshot's system-register lists, `struct mach` and `struct vstate` byte for byte (filled with distinct values), and two device trees. `hvm print` to the init on the redis-oci image: `23c90342d27d6538` with both. The namespace kernel's boot test (`netnsboot`, initramfs `5b634950…` rebuilt from M107's `mkinit.py`): `33ab6e219a6afd5c` with both engines, the recorded value (21,013 exits). M119's lock-step check (M116's Mac table on `explore-ob-redis-oci-arm64`): all 14 groups OK with both, every one of the 37 transcripts identical apart from `secs=`. M121's agent boot check on the Redis agent image: ALL PASS, identical output (boot and RESUME S0 `358eb5c2a491964b`, from S1 twice and fresh twice `ed4703dc275669f0`). Every Mac schedule of docs/REBASELINE.md 9.1 (67 on 19 images) plus four host-token schedules on Redis (`tj=`, `pct=`, `disk=lying:30`, `disk=ioerr:20`), each with `hydo run --image` from a fresh boot once with hvmx and twice with hydo-hvm: **71 of 71 the same RESULT (fingerprint, wfp, stops, typed, inh, ctl, verdict), the Rust pair twice identical**; the ledger-spin runs went through the rewind re-run (M130). The 19 images were rebuilt on this Mac (by a helper agent, no VM): 4 have M140's bytes (ledger, ledger-spin, the voting app, redis-oci) and their 15 schedules give 9.1's recorded fingerprints with both engines; the other 15 differ in bytes because the manifest text is in the image and M140's staging paths of `src:` could not be recovered, so their values are new (all data disks are the recorded ones). `HYDO_HVM=inproc` from a signed copy of `hydo`: `disk=cut | run C=12 R=everysec` on Redis gives the program's RESULT (`0f139f3fc3398595`). Explorations compared by `engine_equiv` (hvmx against hydo-hvm, two workers each): Redis swarm seeds 1–30 (52 runs, 82 consoles; once before and once after the M142 merge), ledger-spin swarm 1–12 (12 runs), the shop with `--strategy process --protocol-faults` 1–16 (16 runs, 21 consoles), the composed plan's racy build 1–8 (28 runs with shrinking, 29 consoles), the voting app on its bridge 1–6 (12 runs): **all IDENTICAL**. After the M144 merge the final engine gave the same netns boot, lock-step and agent-image checks (`lockstep-check.sh` with its new agent groups), in-process run and one schedule per image again (`lockstep-check.sh`: 20 groups OK, among them the agent groups on Redis, `76bce7dce084f41e` clean and `0f139f3fc3398595` with a power cut from S1 twice and fresh twice, and ledger-spin in the rewind mode, `25f1123366ea96c6` and `8dd9c5537321c0e2`, REBASELINE 9.1's values; the 15 distinct images' first schedule the same RESULT as before the merge).
- **Speed** (the Mac shared with another session's VMs; the same work one engine after the other): one schedule with `hydo run` from a fresh boot 11.3 s (hvmx) and 11.5 s (hydo-hvm) on average over the 71; explorations hvmx → hydo-hvm: Redis 424 → 385 s and 229 → 216 s, ledger-spin 121 → 109 s, the shop 83 → 74 s, the composed plan 146 → 120 s, the voting app 290 → 270 s; the lock-step check 381 → 394 s. The two are as fast: a run's time is the guest's and the hash of guest RAM (a serial chain over 1 GiB), which the port does the same way; nothing was made faster at the price of a difference.
- **Checks:** `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked --release --workspace` on the Mac after both merges: 112 test binaries, 353 tests passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored (hydo-config's inventory test included, with `INVENTORY.md` regenerated).
- **Not done, and what deleting the C needs** (AGENTS.md open item 37): the M48 boot fingerprint `81711ada76a4a236` was not taken (its `Image` and initramfs are on the build machine, off limits) and should be, with `hydo-hvm hvm print`, before the C goes; the release tarball is not rebuilt (it ships both engines); then delete `hv/hvm/hvm.c`, `virtio.c`, `virtio_blk.c`, `virtio_net.c`, `virtio.h`, `virtio_int.h`, `spin_observer.c`, `explore/serve.c` and their build scripts (`hv/hvm/build.sh`'s hvm part, `explore/build.sh`), with their users: `hydo/dist/mac/build-release.sh` and `install.sh` (copy and sign hvm and hvmx), `hydo doctor`'s presence check of `hv/hvm/hvm`, `hvm::program`'s fallback to hvmx and `HYDO_HVM=c`, `lockstep-check.sh`'s `ENGINE=c`, `hydo-hvm/tests/c_layout.rs` (record its probe's answers as a golden first, as M137 did with `parse_sched_c.txt`), `hv/hvm/cut-test.sh` and the docs that run `hvm` or `hvmx` by hand (BOOT.md, VIRTIO.md, `explore/README.md`, `spin/RESEARCH.md`, the Mac QUICKSTART). `probe.c` (the M48 hardware probes) is separate and can stay.

### Milestone 141 — DONE (the first third-party project onboarded end to end as an outside user would: a three-node NATS JetStream cluster from a Compose file, with only the skill and the `hydo` command; Jepsen's NATS crash finding found blind and shrunk, its fix passing; the default fsync's loss shown as a configuration finding; fixes to hydo's importer, builder, controller and skill; 2026-11-02)

Branch `worktree-agent-aa4a0ec238e6a3d7f` (from `3a9986e`). Everything ran on this Mac (hvm, M2 Pro), on agent images, with `network: bridge` and the second guest kernel; the bare-metal machine and the build machine were not used. The example is `hydo/onboard/examples/nats-jetstream/` (its RESULTS.md has every table and the friction log).

- **The target, read first.** Jepsen's analysis of NATS 2.12.1 (December 2025), the issues and PRs it names and Synadia's reply: 3.1 (2.10.20–2.10.22: process crashes alone delete the whole stream, "No matching streams for subject", for good; issue 6888, reproduced by Jepsen with `sync_interval` both `always` and default; PR 5946's reproducer: an R3 stream whose three servers are hard-killed right after the stream is added, before the meta layer snapshots; fixed in 2.10.23 by PR 5700, "Don't send meta snapshot when becoming metaleader"), 3.2 and 3.3 (`.blk` and snapshot-file corruption on a minority; open), 3.4 (acknowledged writes lost at a coordinated power loss because the default `sync_interval` flushes every two minutes; documented, not changed), 3.5 (one node's OS crash plus pauses or partitions: lost writes and a lasting split brain; open). Hunted: 3.1 with 2.10.22 against 2.10.23, and 3.4 as a configuration finding (default against `always`). Not hunted: 3.2 and 3.3 (hydo has no file-corruption fault), 3.5 (no power cut of a single service).
- **As an outside user.** A `docker-compose.yaml` as a NATS user writes one (three `nats:<version>-alpine` nodes, one `nats-server.conf` with `server_name: $NATS_NAME`, a named volume on `/data` each, healthchecks on `/healthz?js-enabled-only=true`, `restart: unless-stopped`), then `hydo init`, `hydo compose`, `hydo guide` and its references, `hydo build`, `hydo run`, `hydo explore`, `hydo errors`; hydo's crate sources were read only to fix the gaps below. The Mac release was built from main into a prefix (`hydo/dist/mac/build-release.sh`, the cached assets), plus the second guest kernel from the main checkout and the aarch64 `iproute2`/`iptables` closures fetched with `hydo-nix-fetch` (`HYDO_ARM64_STORE`). The `hydo/` folder: `parallel_driver_publish` (one unique value per command, ack/failed/unknown recorded, an SDK-style `nats.publish_acked` record written to the console), `final_acked_readable` (every acknowledged value readable after the faults; "stream not found" is a violation), `params:` for the release (`nats`) and the configuration file (`conf`), `known-errors.yaml` (the route errors every node prints while its peers start), and a Go test client (`client/`, nats.go v1.37.0, static, both architectures). Six images (2.10.22, 2.10.23, 2.12.1, each with the default fsync and with `always`); a second build gave the same bytes.
- **3.1, found blind.** `hydo explore --seeds 1-50 --strategy process --new-faults` (6 workers; `--more-faults` is x86_64 only): 2.10.22 with the default fsync 14 of 50 fail, every one "stream lost: the cluster says stream jepsen does not exist", the first at seed 1, all reproduced, shrunk in 52 runs to one acknowledged publish and a power cut 30 s later, `disk=cut dseed=4127cc1347fae6ba | run C=30 W=:p1,r1000,cparallel_driver_publish,0.0.0.1390654497` (`8c81413d2915448a` twice); 2.10.23 on the same seeds: no stream lost (13 lose acknowledged messages, which is 3.4, and one read timed out). With `sync_interval: always` (every acknowledged write on the disk, so a power cut is a hard kill of every node, PR 5946's reproducer): 2.10.22 16 of 50, the same minimal schedule (`cc7cca364d1f4fe4`), 2.10.23 0 of 50. Two of those 16 have no power cut and an honest disk; shrunk by hand (the explorer shrinks the first failure of a signature only): `disk=none dseed=a16e4eaefdb58ac0 | run K=n1@15+1 P=n1@1+1 W=5372f125,p3,q1,r1000` (one node paused for a round, later killed; `04d81d362011c8c5`) and `disk=none dseed=890abaea1c4d92d3 | run K=n1@10+2 T=2:-30 W=f4973749,p4,q1,r500` (`eb73e05b4017a2f2`) lose the stream on 2.10.22 with `always` and pass on 2.10.23 and 2.12.1 (both fsync settings) and, by timing, on 2.10.22 with the default fsync. All three nodes killed at once at the first acknowledged publish, by reactions on a record the publish command writes to the console (`disk=none | run A=nats.publish_acked:kill-n1 A=nats.publish_acked:kill-n2 A=nats.publish_acked:kill-n3`): stream lost on 2.10.22 with either fsync (`2fb2fcece2249f37`, `c04c0b1080a18b26`), OK on 2.10.23 and 2.12.1. Every power-cut point (`--sweep cut`, `C=1`..`C=30`) loses the stream on 2.10.22 with `always` (30 of 30) and none on 2.10.23 with `always` (0 of 30). Also `--reactive fault --react-events nats.publish_acked`: 2.10.22 with `always` 23 of 50, 2.10.23 0 of 50; swarm `--new-faults`: 2.10.22 37 of 50 (13 honest-disk stream losses), 2.10.23 37 of 50 with no honest-disk stream loss (12 lost messages; lying-disk and I/O-error classes on both). `hydo repro` of the 2.10.22 exploration: 15 of 15 reproduced.
- **3.4, a configuration finding.** `disk=cut | run C=12`: with the default `sync_interval`, 2.10.23 and 2.12.1 lose 20 of 20 acknowledged messages (`0bc447f697db9622`, `bdc72936b4501190`; the stream survives, empty), with `always` both keep all 20 (`3df83c4ee073946d`, `f43c79941cec2bbd`); 2.10.22 loses the stream with either. `--sweep cut`: the default fsync fails at 30 of 30 cut points on 2.12.1 and on 2.10.23, `always` at 0 of 30 on both. As Redis's `everysec`: documented behaviour of a setting (issue 7564), kept as a build parameter, since the setting needs a restart and so cannot be a knob.
- **Every recorded schedule ran twice from a fresh boot with the same fp and ctl** (RESULTS.md tables: the minimal and aimed schedules on all six images, the fault-free runs).
- **Friction log (the main points; all in RESULTS.md).** Setup: a Mac release lacks the second kernel and the aarch64 network tools (open item 27); only hydo-build's error names `HYDO_ARM64_STORE`. The skill said Python is needed, that the arm64 build refuses `addr:`/`fakes:`/`params:`, and to prefer `--more-faults`, which the Mac explorer refuses ("explore.py: --more-faults needs --backend hvx"). `hydo compose`'s three nodes with their own volume on `/data` would have shared one store, and a hand mount on `/data` was refused. A check's time limit is `test.command_timeout`, not documented (the first power-cut runs ended ERROR at 20 s while the cluster elected leaders). busybox `grep -vxF -f` with an empty pattern file matches every line, so the first check passed "read 0 of 20". Three `K=` tokens killed one node, silently. A reaction never saw a record a composer command printed (it reaches the report, not the console). A check whose last line listed lost ids made every count its own signature. One start-up message is three error kinds (one per node); `hydo errors accept` looks in `hydo-out/explore` by default. No reader or queue checker for NATS; `sync_interval` needs a restart, so it is a build parameter, not a knob; `root.files` has no per-architecture source. The importer's header still names Python-era paths.
- **Fixes to hydo (each its own commit, each with a test).** `9d6e3ec` hydo-build: a data-disk directory may be mounted on an image service's `/data` (`{src: /data/<dir>, dst: /data}`, no `copy_up`), bound once per boot over the data disk's bind (unit test `a_data_disk_directory_on_data`); no existing image changes. `7021c2c` hydo compose: when several services have their own named volume on `/data`, each gets it as its `/data` (one service: as before); new cases `unit-cluster-{default,loopback}`, the eight Sentry cases re-recorded (their redis, seaweedfs, symbolicator and web volumes are now mounted, and those warnings are gone), `HYDO_BLESS` re-records rc, stdout and stderr and records new cases; MANIFEST.md documents `dst: /data`. `acc5e84` hydo-control: a second `K=`, `P=` or `X=` is refused with a message pointing at reactions (HANDOFF decision 13 amended; unit test `a_fault_token_twice_is_refused`); the explorer never draws one, so no recorded schedule changes. `8b52314`, `92085a0` the skill (no Python; arm64 limits; `--more-faults` x86_64 only; one K=/P=/X= per schedule and reactions for several; check time limit; ids out of a check's last line; the busybox grep hazard; reactions and composer records). `60aa783` the example, with the explorer's and controller's identity goldens re-recorded (the controller's test support leaves plans with a restart policy, which its shell model lacks, to restart.rs). `4b477e9`, `ad703b8` re-record hydo-build's, hydo-cli's and hydo-manifest's answers (the example's files, the Compose case list, the skill and MANIFEST.md text; the mutants drawn from the candidate manifests move with them).
- **Checks.** Mac: `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test --locked --release --workspace`: 344 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored (103 test binaries). No engine, module or agent code changed, so no existing image's bytes or fingerprints moved (the builder's new mount is used by no existing manifest; the importer's new mapping changes only the Sentry import cases, which have no image).
- **Left (open item 38).** The explorer reaches 3.1 only through power cuts (one kill per schedule; crashes of every node by reactions, written by hand); 3.2, 3.3 and 3.5 need fault kinds hydo lacks; no x86_64 run; the importer's stale header; reactions do not see composer commands' records; no NATS reader or queue checker; the Mac release still lacks the second kernel and the aarch64 network tools.

### Milestone 145 — DONE (one way to run a guest: the shell images' engine path deleted from both Rust engines and the protocol crate, the pinned reproducers rebuilt as agent images of the stack example with new fingerprints, the explorer's `--branch`, hydo-bench's `--kind stack` and hydo-control's shell-init test models deleted; agent runs byte for byte as before; 2026-11-02)

User decision (2026-11-02): drop the old shell images and the engine code that runs them, keep only agent images, rebuild the two pinned reproducers as agent images with new fingerprints, and drop `--branch` instead of rebuilding it (M43 measured nothing it gives beyond tick jitter). Branch `worktree-agent-a10b5daf819b6bc23` (from `main` = `c04ade3`), with three side branches merged into it (`m145-hvx`, `m145-hvm`, `m145-ctl`). ### Milestone 148 — DONE (one additions-only check for every versioned format: `hydo-schema-compat`, one rule set written down with its reasons and specified by a table of schema changes, the readers as the only per-format option; the project, results and agent-protocol schema tests use it, the two old checkers deleted; 2026-11-03)

Branch `worktree-agent-a64bcc668880f0fdd` (from `main` = `145c456`). No VM, image, module, engine, guest file or format changed; only the tests that guard the formats.

- **The problem.** The additions-only promise of the versioned formats (M114 project, M115 results, M117 agent protocol) was checked by two implementations with different rules: `hydo_manifest::compat::problems` (M114) let a `type` gain kinds and an `anyOf` gain variants at its end, compared only definitions a reference reaches, and required `additionalProperties`, `required` and every bound to stay exactly as they were; `hydo_results::compat::breaking` (M115, also used by the agent protocol's test through a dev-dependency on hydo-results) refused gained kinds and variants outside the root, compared every definition by name (a renamed or removed unreferenced definition failed), ignored `default`, let an enum gain values everywhere and matched root alternatives in any order. Neither said which readers its rules protected.
- **Where it lives.** A new workspace crate `hydo/crates/hydo-schema-compat` (only `serde_json`), a dev-dependency of hydo-manifest, hydo-results and hydo-agent-proto, so no format crate depends on another (hydo-agent-proto's dev-dependency on hydo-results is gone; hydo-agent's own lock file is unchanged, because the dev-dependencies of a path dependency are not in it). API: `check(released, now, &Rules) -> Vec<Problem>`; `Rules::new(Readers::Current | Readers::Released)` and `Rules::open_enum(place)`; a `Problem` has `at` (a JSON pointer into the released schema, `#/$defs/Run/properties/secs`), `kind` (`Narrows`, `Widens`, `Changes`, `UnknownPlace`) and `what`.
- **The two promises, and the one option.** Every format promises that a document the released schema accepts is still accepted with the same meaning (old documents, new readers): a change that refuses such a document narrows the format, a change that reads it differently changes the format, and both always fail. The results format and the agent protocol also promise that readers built for the released schema read what is written now (a CI job reading `result.json`, a released host reading a newer agent's lines). Those readers ignore unknown fields and unknown root alternatives and nothing else (a known field with a value they do not know is an error to `hydo_results::reader` and to `AgentLine::decode`), so for them a widening of a known place fails too (`Readers::Released`). The project format does not promise that: only hydo reads a project, an older hydo refuses a key or value it does not know on purpose, and `hydo_version:` names the release a project needs, so widenings pass (`Readers::Current`). Where a released reader does accept an unknown name, the format names the place open: the agent protocol opens a refusal's `err` (the host keeps the code as text, `ErrorLine::err`) and every command field (`#/$defs/command.*`: the agent refuses an unknown name, but a host sends a new one only to an agent whose hello offers its feature). An open place that names no enum of the released schema is itself a problem, so the option cannot outlive its place.
- **The rules and why** (the crate documentation has them in full):
  - Notes (`description`, `title`, `$comment`, `examples`, `deprecated`, `readOnly`, `writeOnly`) change freely, because no reader acts on them.
  - A new optional property passes for every reader, also in a closed object: no old document has the key (its writer wrote only what the released schema lists), released readers ignore it, and where a reader refuses unknown keys the format has its own gate (`hydo_version:`, hello features).
  - A new required key and a key that became required narrow; a key that stopped being required widens (a released reader may get a document without it).
  - A removed or renamed key changes the format, also in an open object: an old document with it is refused or read without part of its meaning.
  - `type`: a kind gone narrows, a kind gained widens (`integer` counts as part of `number`), a `type` where there was none narrows, a `type` gone widens.
  - `enum`: a value gone narrows, a value gained widens unless the place is open, an `enum` where there was none narrows.
  - `anyOf`/`oneOf` inside a value: every old variant keeps its place, and new variants come only at the end (a widening), because a reader of an untagged choice (serde's `untagged`) takes the first variant that fits; an inserted, reordered or removed variant fails (a moved variant is reported as moved).
  - The root's `anyOf`/`oneOf` (record types, protocol messages): every old alternative must fit some new alternative, anywhere, and new alternatives pass anywhere for every reader. The alternatives are told apart by their own discriminator (`type`, `op`, `ev`), released readers skip unknown record types, a released host keeps an unknown event, and a host sends a new op only to an agent whose hello lists it. (The agent protocol adds a command and its reply in the middle of its root list, so an appended-only rule would refuse every new op.)
  - `$ref`s are followed into `$defs` by name, pairwise and with a cycle guard. A renamed definition passes when what it accepts is compatible, and an unreferenced one is not compared (it accepts no document), because definition names are the generator's (schemars names them after Rust types). A reference written out in place, or an inline schema made a reference, fails (only references are compared with references).
  - `default` may not change or disappear, because it is the meaning of a document that leaves the key out; it may appear only on a property the released schema required.
  - `const`, `format`, `pattern`, `multipleOf`: a new or changed one narrows (the check does not judge whether `uint32` → `uint64` or a rewritten pattern only widens), one gone widens. `uniqueItems: true` added narrows, gone widens.
  - Bounds (`minimum`, `exclusiveMinimum`, `minLength`, `minItems`, `minProperties` and the `max…` ones): tighter or new narrows, looser or gone widens.
  - `additionalProperties`: closing an object narrows; opening a closed one passes (an unknown key is what every reader ignores or what the format's gate handles, as for a new optional key); a map's value schema is compared as a schema. `items` likewise.
  - Every other keyword (`allOf`, `not`, `$schema`, `if`, …) must stay exactly as it was: the check does not judge it, so it allows no change of it.
- **Deliberate differences from the old checkers.** Against M114's: for the project format a required key made optional, an opened object, and a loosened or removed bound, pattern, format or const now pass (all widenings), a root alternative may be added anywhere, and a default may appear only where the key was required (M114 let a default appear anywhere). Against M115's: for results and the agent protocol, gained enum values, kinds and variants and lost `required` entries fail except at named open places (M115 allowed new enum values everywhere, so a new `warn` code, which a released host refuses, would have passed); `default`, bounds, `uniqueItems`, `multipleOf` and unknown keywords are judged (M115 ignored `default` and compared only five assertion keywords); a renamed or unreferenced definition passes (M115 compared every definition by name); a variant inserted inside a value fails (M115 matched any variant anywhere).
- **The format tests.** `hydo-manifest/tests/format.rs` checks the project schema with `Readers::Current`, `hydo-results/tests/schema.rs` the results schema with `Readers::Released`, and `hydo-agent-proto/tests/schema.rs` the agent schema with `Readers::Released` and the two open places; its breaking-change test now also shows that a new refusal code and a new signal name pass and a new `warn` code fails. `hydo/schema/released/` holds exactly these three schemas, so every released schema is checked. The agent-proto README says which names may be added.
- **Deleted.** `hydo/crates/hydo-manifest/src/compat.rs` (284 lines with its 2 unit tests), `hydo/crates/hydo-results/src/compat.rs` (374 lines with its 11 unit tests) and their `pub mod compat`. Every case of their unit tests is a row of the new table (with the verdicts above where the rules differ).
- **The specification.** `hydo-schema-compat/tests/rules.rs` is a table of 70 schema changes on one base schema (a stream of two record types; open and closed objects, a map, an array, an untagged choice, a nullable number with bounds and a format, a defaulted reference, a pattern, a self-referring definition and an unreferenced one), each with its verdict for both kinds of reader (ok, or the place the check must name). The rows cover notes; new optional keys in open and closed objects; new, newly required and no-longer-required keys; removed and renamed keys; types changed, gained, lost, added and removed, and `integer` ↔ `number`; enum values gained (also a record type's discriminator), lost and added; variants appended, inserted, removed and reordered, a choice added or gone; root record types appended, inserted, reordered, removed and changed; definitions renamed, unreferenced ones changed and removed, new ones, referenced ones changed and removed, references written out and made; a change deep inside a self-referring definition; defaults changed, gone, added on an optional key and on a key made optional; const, format and pattern changed, added and gone; unique items; bounds raised, lowered, added and gone; objects opened, opened to a map and closed; map values narrowed and widened; other keys restricted; items changed, gone and accepting nothing; an unjudged keyword added; the draft changed. Four more tests: a released reader refuses everything a current reader refuses; an open place lets its enum gain values and nothing else (prefix places too); an open place that names no enum is a problem; problems carry their kind. `tests/real_schemas.rs` runs the check on the real generators' shapes: every committed and every released schema is an addition to itself, and every committed one to its release, for both kinds of reader; and 1,416 mutations of the three committed schemas (every key of every definition the root reaches removed, every optional key made required, every required key made optional, every enum value removed) are each caught at their place with the right kind.
- **Proofs.** Today's schemas pass against today's released ones under each format's rules (the three format tests) and under both kinds of reader (`real_schemas.rs`); nothing in a format changed. On the Mac, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked --release --workspace` pass (116 test targets, 349 tests, 0 failed); no recorded answer was re-recorded and no file outside the checkers, the three format tests, their crates' manifests and the documents changed (the workspace `Cargo.lock` only gained the new crate and its three users' dev-dependency edges). `cargo metadata --locked --offline` in `hydo/crates/hydo-agent` still accepts that workspace's own lock file.
- **Left.** No release has shipped a format yet, so every `hydo/schema/released/*.json` is still the schema of the milestone that introduced its format (open items 31 and 32). The check judges only the keywords our generators write plus the common assertions; any other keyword must stay as it was, so a generator update that starts writing a new keyword (for example schemars writing `allOf` for a flattened type) fails until the check learns that keyword's rule.

### Milestone 149 — DONE (the Linux release rebuilt and verified for agent images: the release script builds every guest program from the tree and ships the store readers and the gRPC driver generator, its tarball is reproducible, and the tarball installed into clean prefixes on the bare-metal machine runs the quickstart and two repository examples with twice identical fingerprints, as a user and as root, with no Python, Go or Rust on PATH; the released schemas prepared; the version left for the user; 2026-11-04)

Step 2 of the release scope freeze (user, 2026-11-02): nothing new beyond the release itself. Branch `worktree-agent-a7ff2ff9b9d57504b` (from `main` = `3431aaa`). No change to `hvx.c`, `hvx_abi.h`, either engine or the loaded module (main module `B5E97B37504F1A5F508BA30`, not reloaded); the build machine was not used. Own tree on the bare-metal machine `~/hydo-m149` (an rsync of the worktree), results `/var/tmp/m149` (the scripts `build.sh`, `q.sh`, `root.sh`, `ex.sh` and `nopath.sh` are there); every VM went through the module lock (the release's `libexec/hvx-run`, which takes the same `~/.hvx-module.lock`, or `~/bin/hvx-run` for root), at most two at a time, with at least 29 GiB available throughout. M150 rebuilt the Mac release at the same time.

- **The script** (`hydo/dist/linux/build-release.sh`). `HYDO_ASSETS_FROM=DIR` copies the 38 pinned assets from a local directory instead of fetching them from the build machine; the bare-metal machine's `~/hydo-layout-assets` matches every line of `assets.sha256` (the script checks it, as after a fetch). The guest programs are built from the tree into `target/dist-linux` (before, the agent was built into `assets/agent`, which made a second run fail the assets' file count): `guest/hydo-agent` 0.3.0 `398f297e…` (the pin, which hydo-build checks again), `guest/hydo-world` `082592ae…`, and, new, `guest/hydo-read` (`hydo/crates/hydo-read/build.sh`, `64452374…`, the value docs/BUILD-PINS.md gives for this kind of build host) and `guest/hydo-grpc` (`hydo/grpcgen/build-client.sh`, the pinned `3926d137…`). The generator `hydo-grpc-gen` is built with the other programs and shipped as `libexec/hydo-grpc-gen`, started by the new wrapper `bin/hydo-grpc-gen` (`hydo/dist/linux/bin/hydo-grpc-gen`), which sets `HYDO_GRPC_CLIENT` to the release's `guest/` unless it is already set. The tarball is reproducible with GNU tar: `--sort=name --mtime=@1600000000 --owner=root:0 --group=root:0`, `gzip -n -9`, and `umask 022` for the whole script (BSD tar on a Mac keeps the old command and is not reproducible). Two stale comments were removed (the property-table tool and the history-recorder note).
- **The CLI.** On Linux, `hydo build` gives `hydo-build` the release's `guest/hydo-read` (`HYDO_READ_BIN` still overrides it), as the Mac release already did for its arm64 one, and `hydo doctor` checks `guest/hydo-agent` among the release files. `install.sh` makes the two new programs executable. Nothing else in the CLI had to change: since M137 and M144 the release paths, the engine choice (in-process when the device can be opened, else `bin/hydo-hvx` under `libexec/hvx-run sudo`) and the configuration variables were already right.
- **release-prep's WIP (`249aa5a`, M109) was not taken.** It changes `hydo/grpcgen/cmd/hydo-grpc-gen/main.go`, the Go generator that M113 replaced by the Rust `hydo-grpc-gen` and deleted; the Rust generator already takes `--client DIR` and `HYDO_GRPC_CLIENT`, which is what the WIP added. Its goal (open items 22, 23 and 27: ship the generator, its prebuilt client and `hydo-read`) was small without it and is done by the script and CLI lines above; no new pinned asset was needed, because all three are built from source. The branch `release-prep` was left as it is; it is obsolete.

The first pair, before the last documentation changes, gave `ccfceb48…` twice; the final pair gave `3083f40f9abe43aced29c844fc52e189c9adbc2c047d6c853a99bbdeaa5803aa` twice (59,412,744 bytes; 96 files, 131 MB unpacked; `/var/tmp/m149/rel3/` and `rel4/`). ### Milestone 151 — DONE (the public-content fixes before the first release, scope freeze step 3: Apache-2.0 license fields, two machine names and no access details in tracked files, a test that guards it; 2026-11-04)

Decided by the user on 2026-11-04. Nothing new was added; every fingerprint and pinned byte is unchanged.

- **License fields.** The packages outside the workspace that had no license field now say `Apache-2.0` (`sdk/rust`, `sdk/rust-test`, `sdk/rust-test/macros`, the examples `rust-kv` and `redis-composed-rs`). `sdk/python/pyproject.toml` gained `license = {text = "Apache-2.0"}` and the matching classifier. The kernel module keeps its own licenses (`hv/hvx/LICENSE.md`). Not changed: `sdk/js/package.json` (`UNLICENSED`), because the node-kv example stages that file into its images, so the field is part of the node-kv image bytes and fingerprints on both engines (open item 41); the Go SDK has no metadata file (Go has no license field), and a comment line in its sources would move line numbers inside the order service's binary.
- **Proof that no guest program changed.** Built on this Mac with their build scripts before the change and again after it from clean target directories (`hydo-agent/build.sh all`, `hydo-read/build.sh all`, `hydo-world/build.sh` for both architectures, `hydo/grpcgen/build-client.sh amd64 arm64`): every file the same bytes, and each equals its pin in docs/BUILD-PINS.md: hydo-agent `398f297e…` / `099e5444…`, hydo-read (Mac build) `2b4d6a62…` / `88576fa8…`, hydo-world `082592ae…` / `fefcca66…`, hydo-grpc `3926d137…` / `fd762fa0…`. The Rust SDK examples (`rust-kv` with `build-rkv.sh`, `redis-composed-rs` with the same flags; both architectures) also gave the same bytes before and after. Cargo's `-C metadata` does not cover the license field.
- **Machines.** Tracked files now call the two machines only "the bare-metal machine" (runs hvx) and "the build machine" (builds guest images; optional since M140). Removed from every tracked file: remote-shell commands, logins and user names of the machines, machine home paths, and the older nicknames ("the box", "the build box", "the bare-metal test machine"; manifest comments that say "build box" stay, because their bytes are inside images).
- **How scripts reach a machine.** The tracked `machines.sh` at the repository root is sourced by every script that works on a machine (`dev.sh`, `hv/hvx/deploy-metal.sh`, `lockstep-metal.sh`, the side-module builders in `hv/hvx/{avx,fastturn,gc,pt,smp,smp2,tdet}`, `hv/hvx/pt/build-ptstack.sh`, `hv/hvx/safety/safety.sh` and `side-check.sh`, `hydo/crates/hydo-agent/bare-metal.sh`, both release scripts, the node-kv and python-kv fetch scripts). It reads the git-ignored `machines.local.sh` next to it (in a git worktree without its own copy, the main checkout's; `HYDO_MACHINES` names another file), which defines `BARE_METAL` and `on_bare_metal`, `BUILD_MACHINE` and `on_build_machine`; `need_bare_metal`, `need_build_machine` and `need_nix_machine` stop a script with a message that names the file and the missing definition. The scripts' environment variables that named a machine are gone; `HVX_METAL_TREE` stays, and `HYDO_NIX_MACHINE=bare-metal` makes the release and fetch scripts copy the Nix store paths from the bare-metal machine instead of the build machine. `build-ptstack.sh` copies the program between the two machines through this computer instead of with forwarded credentials. The scripts work in POSIX sh too (the release scripts).
- **The rule and its test.** AGENTS.md "Safety and coordination rules" has the rule ("Machines in tracked files"), in generic words only. `cargo test -p hydo-agents --test public_content` reads every file `git ls-files` lists. Generic patterns, outside recorded fixtures, goldens and result examples: a remote-shell or remote-copy command, an IPv4 address outside 0/8, 10/8, 127/8, the 255.x netmasks and the documentation ranges, and the hosting company's words; two files are allowed with their reasons (the syzkaller test VM's own sshd, and the composer's dotted seed lists in `hydo-control/tests/m123.rs`). Concrete values: the git-ignored `AGENTS.local.md` keeps a marked list of the real aliases, addresses, logins and names; when the file exists (in a worktree without its own copy, the main checkout's), the test fails if any tracked file at all contains one of them as a word, and without it that part is skipped. A second test proves the patterns and the list parser catch and pass the intended lines. Before the commit, `git grep -i -w -F` of every listed value found nothing.
- **Proof on the machines.** On the bare-metal machine, reached through `machines.local.sh`, in a tree of this session's own (`HVX_METAL_TREE=hydo-m151`), with the loaded main module (no reload, no module source changed): `hydo/crates/hydo-agent/bare-metal.sh hydo-m151 -- cargo test --locked` copied the repository there and ran the agent's native tests (10 passed, 1 ignored), and then `hv/hvx/deploy-metal.sh` reported "ALL PASS (33 checks)", with both pinned reproducers (`8fc461db23ef6642` VIOLATION, `aad6a563e2046361` OK) and every recorded fingerprint. A first `deploy-metal.sh` into the empty new tree failed to compile, because the script copies only the engine sources and the crates, not the module header or the files `hydo-agents` builds in (as before M151; the main tree has them). Without `machines.local.sh`, or with a file that lacks a definition, `lockstep-metal.sh`, `dev.sh` and the Linux release script stop at once with the message that names the file.
- **Goldens.** Only the two `hydo guide manifest` answers of `hydo-cli/tests/golden/cli.jsonl` changed (MANIFEST.md is built into the binary).
- **Checks:** `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked --release --workspace` on the Mac: 117 test binaries, 351 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored.
- **Left** (open item 41): the node-kv package's license field, the Mac programs' panic paths, freeze results of M73/M76/M92 that do not name their system, and the release tarballs built before this milestone.
